# Director of Customer Data & Data Science

# **Join Readly!**

Readly was built on a simple but powerful idea: that curious people should never have to choose between the publications they love and the ones they haven't discovered yet. One subscription. Thousands of titles. Journalism, culture, lifestyle, science, sport, and ideas from around the world, available on any screen, at any moment.

Readly is now part of Cafeyn Group. With the acquisition of Readly's non-Nordic operations, Cafeyn further strengthens its position as the European leader in access to information – combining scale, technology, and deep local market expertise.

Together, the Group now operates across 15 markets, serves 2.5 million users, and provides access to more than 5,200 publications from 1,100 partner publishers.

To empower individuals with access to trusted, high-quality content that fosters personal growth and discovery. Whether it's through the comprehensive collection of news and features on Cafeyn & Readly, the digital publishing solutions of Milibris, the fun and educative content for children on Kidjo, or the collections for manga lovers by Mangas.io, Cafeyn Group stands at the forefront of digital content experiences.

If you're passionate about building strategic partnerships, driving commercial growth and shaping the future of digital media, we'd love to meet you.

As Cafeyn continues to grow, the Group is accelerating its transformation towards a truly data-driven organization, leveraging Customer Data and Artificial Intelligence to improve business performance, enhance product innovation and develop new revenue streams.

As Director of Customer Data & Data Science, you will define and lead Cafeyn Group's Customer Data strategy, transforming data into a strategic asset that drives business decisions, product development and revenue growth.

Reporting into the Group's leadership structure, you will act as the primary ambassador for Customer Data, working closely with the Executive Committee, Marketing, Product, Content, Business and Technology teams.

Your mandate will be twofold: maximize the business value of customer data and accelerate the development of AI-powered products.

Beyond delivering insights and tools, you will challenge existing business practices, identify opportunities for improvement and ensure that data becomes a driver of strategic decision-making rather than simply a reporting function.

You will lead the restructured Data Analysis and Data Science teams, establish the foundations for scalable Data adoption, and work closely with Data Engineering to ensure the reliability, accessibility and performance of Cafeyn's data infrastructure.

## **Your responsibilities**

### **1. Define the Customer Data strategy and drive business performance**

* Define and implement Cafeyn Group's Customer Data strategy, aligned with the Group's overall business priorities and growth ambitions.
* Act as the primary representative of Customer Data at Executive Committee level, translating strategic priorities into actionable data initiatives and measurable business outcomes.
* Develop a comprehensive understanding of customer behaviour, engagement, retention and monetization across Cafeyn's B2C, B2B2C, B2B and CDS business models.
* Ensure that business teams have access to reliable, relevant and actionable dashboards, analyses and performance indicators to identify challenges, understand underlying trends and improve business performance.
* Structure KPI frameworks and performance funnels across Marketing, Product, Content and Business, identifying opportunities to optimize acquisition, engagement, conversion, retention and revenue.
* Develop predictive capabilities, particularly churn prevention models, to anticipate customer behaviour and enable proactive retention strategies.
* Challenge business stakeholders constructively, moving beyond a traditional internal service-provider relationship to become a strategic business partner who questions assumptions and helps identify new opportunities.
* Establish robust data governance policies, ensuring data quality, integrity, accessibility and consistent usage across the organization.
* Drive data literacy and foster a data-driven culture, empowering teams to incorporate data into their day-to-day decisions.

### **2. Develop the data monetization strategy**

* Define Cafeyn's Customer Data monetization strategy, supporting the diversification of the Group's revenue streams.
* Identify opportunities to create value from first-party data, audience insights and customer segmentation, particularly in relation to advertising and B2B commercial offerings.
* Build the data foundations required for effective audience activation, including identity resolution, tagging, segmentation and measurement.
* Work closely with Marketing, Sales, Business and Content teams to translate customer insights into new commercial opportunities and scalable revenue-generating initiatives.
* Assess the potential of data products and services, ensuring that monetization initiatives are commercially relevant, technically feasible and aligned with applicable privacy and regulatory requirements.

### **3. Lead Data Science, AI-powered product innovation and experimentation**

* Lead Cafeyn's Data Science capability, managing a team of 2–3 Data Scientists responsible for developing and deploying AI-driven product features.
* Define the Data Science roadmap in close collaboration with Product and Technology leadership, ensuring that initiatives address meaningful customer needs and deliver measurable value.
* Establish the processes, methodologies and operating conditions required to accelerate the delivery, deployment and continuous improvement of Data Science developments.
* Oversee the evolution of AI-powered product capabilities, including personalized recommendations, the automated daily digest feature, semantic search and future content discovery innovations.
* Ensure that Data Science initiatives are prioritized according to their expected impact, feasibility and alignment with Cafeyn's product strategy.
* Drive the transition from experimentation to production, improving delivery predictability, model performance and the operational impact of AI-powered features.
* Partner closely with Product teams to measure the impact of AI innovations on engagement, retention, customer satisfaction and business performance.
* Own the tooling and technical enablement of Cafeyn's A/B testing framework, using Statsig to support a scalable, quantitative experimentation capability.
* Work closely with Product teams, who own the testing strategy and prioritization, to ensure that the underlying tooling enables reliable experiments, robust statistical analysis and informed product decisions.
* Establish clear measurement practices to evaluate the impact of AI initiatives and experimentation on operational efficiency and product performance.

### **4. Partner with Data Engineering to build scalable data foundations**

* Act as the primary internal interface between Customer Data, Data Science and the Data Engineering team, ensuring that the data platform meets current and future business needs.
* Work closely with Data Engineering leadership to assess whether the existing architecture can support Cafeyn's strategic ambitions, growing data volumes and evolving analytical requirements.
* Define data availability, reliability, integrity and completeness requirements, establishing clear service-level agreements (SLAs) and access policies.
* Ensure that the right data is accessible to the right teams, through the appropriate tools and within the required timeframes, from real-time applications to historical and cold-storage environments.
* Guide decisions around data accessibility, storage costs and platform scalability, ensuring that infrastructure choices support both advanced analytics and production-grade AI applications.
* Anticipate the data requirements of new business models, customer activation initiatives and AI-powered product features, aligning the data roadmap with the broader Technology strategy.

### **5. Build and develop high-performing teams**

* Lead and develop the restructured Product Data and Data Science organization, bringing together complementary analytical, machine learning and product innovation capabilities.
* Manage a team comprising two Senior Data Analysts, one Machine Learning expert focused on predictive modelling, and a Data Science team of 2–3 specialists.
* Establish clear priorities, ownership, delivery processes and performance expectations across the teams.
* Foster collaboration between Data Analysis, Data Science, Data Engineering, Product and Business stakeholders.

# About CodeSpeak

CodeSpeak is an Agentic Engineering Toolkit: a set of tools to make AI coding work well for production-grade software projects.

Coding agents are amazing for prototypes, one-offs, and hobby projects. Yet, for serious production, results are more mixed:

* the amount of slop in codebases is growing, and they become less and less maintainable (GitClear-26),
* people can’t keep up with reviews,
* and more and more areas in projects accumulate “comprehension debt” (nobody really understands how they work).

As a result, engineering leaders are seeing more incidents per PR (+23.5%, see Cortex-26). In other words, **people ship slop, and it’s starting to bite them**. “The Claude Code moment” happened in late 2025, so what we see today is not even the full extent of the consequences.

At CodeSpeak, we believe three simple things:

* AI coding tools can help people make quality production software;
* Nobody wants to ship slop, people just don’t have the right tools to remain on top of their codebases;
* While coding may be solved by models, Software Engineering is still a human job.

**CodeSpeak’s Vision**. The prompts we give to coding agents are a new proto-language that is emerging right now. And we want to make it into a good, usable production language. The valuable part is that these prompts contain the intent behind the code. The resulting code can be generated from it, therefore it must be a complete description of the system. Right now, this description is very messy, and we want to make it clean and useful.

**CodeSpeak’s Current Approach**. We believe that user intent is the real primary artifact, and code is just what's derived from it. Right now, we're building an engine that captures this intent from session transcripts, distills it into structured requirements, grounds them in the code, and enforces them as the codebase changes.

These requirements become the layer developers actually work through, across the entire development process. For example:

* When an agent starts a new feature, CodeSpeak injects the relevant requirements into its context, so it builds with the rest of the system in mind.
* When a new prompt in a chat contradicts older requirements, a code isn’t written until the conflict is resolved.
* Code review starts from the requirement-level diff: what intent changed, what constraints were added or removed, and whether the implementation still satisfies them.

See more in our blog, and this is only the beginning. Let’s talk about what will come next when we meet.

# Team

CodeSpeak is founded by Andrey Breslav, creator of Kotlin – a language used by millions of developers every day. # Research Associate or Research Fellow in Computational Health Policy Modelling

**Build the Next Generation of Health Policy Simulation Models**

Do you want your research to influence how governments design policies to prevent chronic disease? Are you excited by the challenge of combining data, simulation, and policy to tackle the world’s biggest health problems?

The Centre for Health Economics & Policy Innovation (CHEPI) at Imperial Business School is seeking a Research Associate / Research Fellow in Computational Health Policy Modelling to play a central role in developing Health-GPS — our state-of-the-art microsimulation model for non-communicable disease (NCD) policy analysis. Appointment will be made at Research Associate or Research Fellow level, depending on experience.

**Why This Role Matters**

Chronic diseases such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease remain leading causes of illness and premature death worldwide. Yet, the tools available to evaluate and design effective prevention policies are still evolving. *Health-GPS* provides a framework to explore how changes in diet, physical activity, and related risk factors affect long-term population health and economic outcomes.

*Health-GPS* represents the gradual accumulation and interaction of individual-level risk factors — such as BMI, diet, and income — offering insights into the potential impact of different policy interventions over time.

You will help develop and apply this model across major international projects including:

* **GOLDFINCH** – estimating the effects of fiscal policies on ultra-processed food consumption.
* **JA Prevent NCD** – a European Joint Action on integrated strategies for NCD prevention.
* **JACARDI** – a European initiative to reduce cardiovascular and diabetes risk.

**What You’ll Do**

* Contribute to the architecture, development, optimisation, and maintenance of Health-GPS, writing and reviewing code in its C++ codebase and ensuring its continued scientific and policy relevance.
* Work with colleagues to plan and deliver modelling work across multiple projects, producing high-quality outputs on time.
* Help integrate new methodologies, including AI and machine-learning approaches, into simulation design.
* Conduct quantitative analyses to estimate the health and economic impact of proposed policies.
* Identify and manage relevant datasets in collaboration with internal and external partners.
* Communicate findings through academic papers, policy briefs, and stakeholder workshops.
* Contribute to funding proposals and the expansion of CHEPI’s modelling activities.

**What We’re Looking For**

We’re seeking a creative and technically strong individual with:

* A PhD (or equivalent, or near completion) in health economics, epidemiology, computer science, or a related field.
* Experience building or using microsimulation models or other quantitative policy tools.
* Strong programming skills in at least one language (e.g. Python, R, or C++), and experience contributing to a shared codebase using version control (e.g. git).
* Experience working with large or longitudinal datasets.
* The ability to translate complex model outputs into actionable policy insights.

Experience with C++ is highly desirable. Experience applying AI or ML methods to health or policy modelling is also desirable.

Candidates for appointment as Research Fellow should also demonstrate a strong publication record, experience contributing to funding proposals, and the ability to design and lead original research.

**How to Apply**

Interested? Please read the job description and person specification, then apply online with:

* A cover letter explaining your motivation and relevant experience, and indicating the level (Research Associate or Research Fellow) for which you are applying.
* Your CV.
* Contact details for two referees.

This position is full-time and fixed-term for 24 months, with potential for extension depending on funding.

For queries, contact Prof. Franco Sassi (f.sassi@imperial.ac.uk)

* A widened connector road from M60 northbound to M60 westbound – replacing the current single lane with two lanes

# Midweight Designer

**Team Luke Powell and Jody Hudson-Powell, Pentagram London**

Full time and permanent. London studio, three days in and two remote. £40,000 to £50,000 depending on experience.

## The practice

Luke and Jody have worked together for twenty years, ten of them at Pentagram. Before that it was the two of them, a desk, a laser printer and whoever they could pull in for a project. There was no point employing an animator when the next three jobs might not need animation.

The team is bigger now and it is built the same way. Most people here can animate, code, draw and design, and we still don't know which discipline the next job will want.

We're a design studio that happens to work on brands. Design leads. Strategy matters and we do plenty of it, but how a thing looks and moves and behaves is the argument rather than the packaging.

The work is deliberately unsorted. Isomorphic Labs, Cohere, Graphcore, Intrinsic, Oxford Ionics and Stereolabs sit next to Total War: Warhammer III, Channel 4, Cartier, four seasons of London Fashion Week, Frieze, MoN Takanawa: The Museum of Narratives, Bait and Happy Face Pizza. We don't sort them into categories. What we learn making an exhibition ends up in a robotics company, and it goes the other way just as often.

What connects them is simplification. We like a messy brief, where a company has lost coherence or never had it, and the instinct is to find the one system that makes everything else fall into place. Getting there usually means building something first. A tool, a typeface, a generative process. Ideas start analogue, in sketchbooks and arguments, and if you can't draw it or say it then it isn't ready. Then we make it, and the medium usually tells us what the idea actually was.

## The role

A midweight designer with a strong core in brand and typography, and growing fluency in motion.

Midweight here is about autonomy rather than years. It means you can take a brief from concept to something presentable without a director sitting next to you, and you know when to come back and ask.

You'd be working to Luke and Jody, alongside two Producers, five Designers, two Motion Designers and a Team Assistant.

## The work

* Building visual systems that adapt and behave
* Typography and layout, at a high standard, across a lot of different sectors
* Following one idea across brand narrative, graphic design, motion and interface to see where it holds
* Working with the motion and 3D team, and often with creative coders
* Pitches and new business, which come round more often than you might expect

## The toolkit

**Weekly:** Figma, Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign, After Effects.

**Also in use somewhere in the team:** Cinema 4D, Blender, Glyphs, Houdini, Unity, Unreal, and a lot of front-end code.

We don't expect anyone to arrive with all of that. We hire based on how quickly someone picks up a tool, so if you've taught yourself something awkward recently, show us that.

On AI, we use it daily and always in a deliberate manner. We apply critical thinking and judgement to all our ways of working.

## What you might find hard

Briefs move. Clients change their minds. A fair proportion of what you make won't get used, and some of it will have been good. You'll also switch categories fast, so a robotics company one week and a museum the next. Some people find that energising and some find it tiring, and it's worth being honest with yourself about which.

## What we'll do

* Pay you £40,000 to £50,000 depending on experience, reviewed every year, with rises tied to progression
* Give you regular time with Luke, Jody and your design lead, not only when something has gone wrong
* Put your name on the work, internally and externally
* Fund training and conferences where they're relevant to what you're building
* Cover 20 days holiday to start, rising to 25 over 5 years service, plus a Christmas closure and bank holidays
* Pension, Medicash and Cycle to Work
* Feed you. Chef Musa cooks a delicious and nutritious lunch in the studio

## To apply

Portfolio and CV to workwithteamjl@pentagram.com. Subject line: **Midweight Designer Application**.

We'd like a mix of commercial brand work, conceptual work, and things you made for yourself.

For every project, tell us plainly what you did and what other people did. We would rather see honest attribution on a rough project than a polished one where we can't understand your involvement.

And answer this in under 150 words:

> Show us one project where the system did something you hadn't fully planned for. What happened, and what did you do about it.

## How we hire

Roughly three stages, usually inside three weeks.

1. We read your work and your answer to the question above
2. If shortlisted, a conversation with Luke, Jody and a designer from the team
3. A possible paid exercise, if applicable, briefed properly, discussed in a follow-up session

We'll tell you the format and who you're meeting before each stage. We're a small team and we read everything, but we can only reply to shortlisted applicants.

We don't require a design degree and we're genuinely interested in people who arrived here sideways. If you need anything adjusted at any stage, including extra time, questions in advance, or a different format, tell us when you apply and we'll sort it. It won't count against you.

We'll also cover travel to interviews within the UK.

Pentagram is an equal opportunity employer. We particularly want to hear from people under-represented in design and technology.

Email your application

Pentagram is a multi-disciplinary, independently owned design studio.

Our work encompasses graphics and identity, strategy and positioning, products and packaging, exhibitions and installations, websites and digital experiences, advertising and communications, data visualizations and typefaces, sound and motion. Our 23 partners are all practicing designers, and whether working collaboratively or independently, they do so in friendship.

Our structure is unique. We are the only major design studio where the owners of the business are the creators of the work and serve as the primary contact for every client. This reflects our conviction that great design cannot happen without passion, intelligence and—above all—personal commitment, and is demonstrated by a portfolio that spans five decades, many industries, and clients of every size.

### **What you will do**

* **Corporate Identity & Access Management (IAM):** Design, optimize, and support corporate IAM structures, including group architectures, identity system integration, and streamlined employee onboarding/offboarding workflows.

* Practical experience establishing or executing standardized vendor technical security assessments.
* Background in supporting security incident response and handling daily security alert triage.
* A strong bias for automation and an eagerness to leverage AI tools or agentic scanning mechanisms within corporate security workflows.

* Hands-on experience building or integrating AI-driven automation, agentic workflows, or custom scripts for security operations.

**Determined**Determined at Iso is the way we pursue our goal. It’s a confidence in our hypothesis, as well as the urgency and agility needed to deliver on it. Because disease won’t wait, so neither should we.

**Together**Together at Iso is about connection, collaboration across fields and catalytic relationships. It’s knowing that transformation is a group project, and remembering that what we’re doing will have a real impact on real people everywhere.

We believe that to be successful we need a team with a range of skills and talents. We value unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, and perspectives, and harness these qualities to create extraordinary impact.

It’s hugely important for us to share knowledge and build strong relationships with each other, and we find it easier to do this if we spend time together in person. **Job Title**:  SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central (EC) Lead

**Location:**  UK (Maidenhead / hybrid; regular client site presence)

**Position Type**:  Full-time

**Experience Level:** 10-14 years

**Role Overview**

We are seeking an experienced SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central (EC) Lead to own the EC solution on a large-scale SuccessFactors and Employee Central Payroll (ECP) transformation. The programme migrates a complex UK public sector payroll and HR estate from SAP HCM on S/4HANA into the SAP SuccessFactors landscape, covering approximately 65,000 employee and pensioner records, 17 payrolls, multiple public sector pension schemes (LGPS, Teachers, NHS), external employers paid on the client's payroll, and a significant multiple-employment population.

Employee Central is the system of record for the programme. It goes live first, alongside Recruiting and Onboarding, and then becomes the source of employee data for Employee Central Payroll. For several months between those go-lives EC runs alongside the existing SAP payroll, so the EC design has to work for both. The EC Lead owns the EC design end to end and is the client's main point of contact for EC design decisions, covering the organisation structure, position management, job and pay data, employee lifecycle events, custom data objects, role-based permissions and data retention.

  

### Requirements

Key Responsibilities

* EC solution ownership. Own the Employee Central solution end to end, from fit-to-standard and detailed design through configuration workbooks, build, testing and go-live, and take accountability for EC design sign-off at each programme milestone.

* Client design leadership. Lead EC design workshops with HR, payroll, finance and IT stakeholders, present options with a clear recommendation, record decisions, and drive open questions to closure with named owners and dates.

* Foundation and organisation structure. Design legal entities, business units, divisions, departments, locations, cost centres, pay groups and pay structures, including the UK legal entity fields (for example PAYE reference and Accounts Office reference) that SAP does not deliver as standard. The client is redesigning its organisation in parallel, so the structure must absorb change without rework.

* Position management. Design position management and the reporting hierarchy, including how the hierarchy is built during migration where the legacy system holds little position-to-position reporting.

* Employee data and lifecycle. Design job information, compensation and pay components, and the employee lifecycle (hire, rehire, transfer, job and pay change, termination), with event reasons, workflows and business rules.

* Complex populations. Design how EC handles:

* Multiple and concurrent employments

* External employers paid on the client's payroll

* Pensioner populations held in EC without an active position

* Employees moving between payrolls and employers

* Extensibility. Design custom MDF objects for client-specific data held today in custom infotypes (for example teacher qualifications and status), and agree with the client what is carried forward and what is retired.

* Permissions and data protection. Design role-based permissions with the client, and the data retention and purge approach (DRTM) that meets UK GDPR and the client's statutory retention rules.

* Payroll and integration alignment. Agree with the ECP Lead and the integration team the EC data that payroll depends on, and the EC to payroll replication approach, including the period when EC is live but payroll still runs on the existing SAP system.

* Data migration. Work with the data migration team on EC load templates, field mapping, transformation rules and reconciliation across each data cycle, and confirm EC data quality before each load.

* Recruiting and Onboarding fit. Make sure the EC design supports the Recruiting and Onboarding modules going live alongside it, including position, job and new hire data flowing into EC.

* Testing, cutover and hypercare. Support system integration testing and UAT, own EC defect resolution, prepare and run the EC cutover activities, and lead EC through hypercare and stabilisation.

* Team leadership. Lead and quality-assure the work of the EC configuration consultants, set configuration and documentation standards, and review all EC build before it goes into test.

* Governance and reporting. Report EC progress, risks and decisions to the programme leadership and steering forums, and support architecture assurance and change control throughout the delivery lifecycle. Technical Skills & Experience

**Technical Skills & Experience**

* Deep hands-on Employee Central configuration: foundation objects, Corporate and Succession data models, country-specific fields, picklists, MDF and generic objects, Business Rules and workflows.
* Position management, including position hierarchy design, Position Org Chart, and the rules that keep positions and employee job data in step.
* Role-based permissions design, including permission groups, target populations and field-level access.
* EC data loads and validation using Import Employee Data, MDF import and export, Integration Center and the OData API.
* Data Retention Management (DRTM) and UK GDPR design in SuccessFactors.
* Understanding of how EC feeds Employee Central Payroll, and the EC data payroll relies on (pay components, cost assignment, multiple employments).
* Working knowledge of SAP HCM (PA and OM infotypes) to map the legacy design and data into EC.
* SAP Activate, configuration workbooks, and managing the twice-yearly SuccessFactors release cycle.

**Essential Experience**

* At least two full-lifecycle Employee Central implementations in a lead or solution architect role
* Leading client-facing design workshops and owning design sign-off
* Position management and complex organisation structure design
* Role-based permissions and data protection design
* Migration from SAP HCM on-premise to Employee Central
* Leading and reviewing the work of a configuration team

**Desirable Experience**

* UK public sector or local government HR (for example councils, schools and academies, pension funds)
* Employee Central integrated with Employee Central Payroll
* Multiple and concurrent employment design
* Recruiting and Onboarding integration with EC
* People Analytics (Stories) reporting on EC data
* Organisation redesign delivered during a live implementation

**Certifications**

* **Essential**: Current SAP certification in SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Core, kept up to date through SAP Learning Hub.
* **Desirable**: SAP SuccessFactors certification in a second module, for example Recruiting, Onboarding or Employee Central Payroll.

**Soft Skills**

* Confident with senior client stakeholders, and able to challenge and hold a design position
* Clear decision-making and the ability to explain trade-offs in plain language
* Strong written communication for design documents and decision records
* Coaching and quality review of less experienced consultants
* Attention to detail appropriate to data that drives payroll
* Ability to manage competing priorities across parallel workstreams

## About us

We're reverse-engineering the origin of life — one of the great unsolved problems in science, and one we think AI finally makes tractable. Understanding this transition, from geochemistry to biochemistry, is what will let us orchestrate molecular networks and build systems that are more capable, adaptive, and efficient.

If we succeed, the applications are vast: catalysis, green synthesis, ab initio synthetic biology, programmable matter. Understanding and harnessing these processes could let ten billion of us thrive on this planet — and let life keep evolving beyond it.

We're a small, diverse team of AI engineers, computational scientists, and bench scientists. We hold ourselves to the rigor of a research institute, but we ship like an engineering firm. Global team, HQs in Cambridge, MA and London, UK.

**The role**

You'll engineer proteins to carry out useful chemistry, combining enzyme discovery, directed evolution, and experimental characterisation. You'll own the experimental cycle: choosing starting points, building variant libraries, developing screens, and establishing which changes improve function and why.

This is a hands-on role working closely with our computational and ML teams. You'll test designed proteins at the bench, use experimental results to guide subsequent rounds, and develop enzymes with the activity, selectivity, and stability needed for their intended application. There’s no fixed screening pipeline to inherit — you'll help decide how we build it.

**What you'll do**

* Design and run protein engineering campaigns, from initial enzyme selection and library design through screening and characterisation of improved variants.
* Build and express variant libraries using site-directed, random, and combinatorial mutagenesis.
* Develop assays and high-throughput screens that reliably measure the properties we're trying to improve.
* Express, purify, and characterise proteins, measuring kinetics, substrate scope, selectivity, and stability under relevant reaction conditions.
* Work with computational scientists to test proposed designs, interpret successes and failures, and use the results to guide the next round.
* Develop enzymatic reactions and cascades, identifying how enzyme performance, cofactors, and reaction conditions affect overall productivity.

**Essential experience**

We're interested in the engineering campaigns you've run, the assays you've built, and what you learned from them. We care about:

* A track record of improving protein or enzyme function through directed evolution or rational engineering.
* Practical fluency in molecular biology, including cloning, library construction, mutagenesis, and recombinant protein expression.
* Experience developing and troubleshooting enzyme assays and screening workflows, with appropriate controls and follow-up validation.
* A solid grasp of enzyme mechanism, kinetics, and structure–function relationships, and the ability to use these to guide experiments.
* Experience independently taking projects through multiple design–build–test cycles and explaining what drove the results.

**Highly preferred**

* Experience with industrial biocatalysis or engineering enzymes for demanding reaction conditions.
* Experience integrating liquid handling and laboratory automation with high-throughput screening.
* Familiarity with biosensor-based screens, growth-based selection, or FACS.
* Experience testing computationally designed proteins and feeding experimental results back into design.
* Experience with enzyme cascades, fermentation, or transferring enzymatic processes from the bench to larger scales.

## Logistics

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Junior Local Financial Accountant to join our finance team. * Managing and resolving finance-related queries from internal stakeholders

* Identifying opportunities for process improvements and increased efficiencies

Previous experience in a finance or accounting role is desirable, alongside strong Excel skills, experience using financial systems, and a high level of numerical accuracy and attention to detail. You will be organised, able to manage competing priorities, and comfortable working to deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

We are looking for someone who is naturally curious and enjoys understanding the story behind the numbers. **Doodle is a B2B SaaS platform used by millions of professionals to coordinate meetings and collaboration across teams and companies. ### **The Role**

**In this role, you’ll co-own a share of the analytics layer that powers decisions across Doodle. You’ll turn raw product data into trusted, scalable datasets for experimentation, reporting and product innovation. Our transformations are built in dbt on top of Amazon Redshift, with Athena alongside it, and teams explore and report on data in Power BI, Hex and our own internal AI tools.**

**You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Finance and Leadership. Some days that means defining the metrics the whole company runs on. Other days it means helping a Growth Manager design an A/B test, or showing a team how to answer their own questions without waiting on anyone. If you get excited by clean models, well-defined metrics and data people actually trust, you’ll find a stimulating environment here.**

**AI is at the heart of how we work. We expect you to use AI coding tools to move faster on modelling, testing and documentation, and to help the rest of Doodle get more out of AI in their daily work with data.**

### **What You’ll Actually Do**

* **Model the Data: Design, build and maintain scalable analytics data models in dbt, following analytics engineering best practices.**
* **Own Data Quality: Build reliable transformations from raw product data to business-ready datasets, with testing, validation and documentation across the analytics layer.**
* **Define the Metrics: Define, document and maintain the trusted business metrics used across the company, and keep definitions aligned across teams.**
* **Build the Semantic Layer: Evolve a scalable semantic layer that makes consistent reporting and self-service analytics possible.**

* **Enable Self-Service: Build dashboards and reports in Power BI, Hex or our internal AI tools, and coach stakeholders so they can find their own answers.**
* **Lead with AI: Build AI-enabled analytics workflows and help teams across Doodle adopt AI in how they work with data.**

### **What do you bring?**

**You’ll thrive here if you combine strong analytics engineering fundamentals with a product and business mindset, and you’re honest about your strengths, gaps and what you’re still learning.**

* **The Modelling Experience: Strong, hands-on experience building analytics data models with dbt or a similar transformation framework, and a good grasp of dimensional modelling.**
* **The SQL: Advanced SQL skills and experience working with large analytical datasets.**
* **The Warehouse: Experience with cloud data warehouses such as Amazon Redshift.**
* **The BI Toolkit: Experience building dashboards and self-service reports in Power BI or similar BI tools.**
* **The Product Lens: Familiarity with experimentation frameworks and product analytics.**
* **The AI Mindset: Hands-on experience with Claude or similar AI assistants, including setting up MCPs and using AI coding tools. You’ve helped drive AI adoption in a team or organisation.**
* **The Communicator: You can explain technical concepts to technical and non-technical people alike, and turn data into recommendations that help stakeholders decide.**
* **The Location: You are based in, and have the right to work in, the country where this role is advertised. We cannot sponsor visas or support relocation at this time.**

* **Experience building semantic layers or self-service analytics platforms.**
* **Good Python skills for data processing and automation, for example with pandas.**
* **Familiarity with workflow orchestration tools such as Airflow, and experience with Athena.**
* **Experience with tools such as Google Analytics 4, GrowthBook (A/B testing) or Avo (tracking plan design and data governance).**
* **The SaaS Background: Experience working in a modern B2B SaaS environment.**

* **Real Impact: Your models shape how the world meets.**
* **Technical Stretch: We deal with “Time” problems most companies never meet, and the product data that comes with them: time zones, calendars and schedules that keep changing.**
* **Measurable Impact: With millions of users, the data you model drives decisions you’ll see play out in real numbers.**

**Due to the nature of the work and the customers we support, the successful candidate must be eligible to meet UK Government and contractual personnel security requirements, including the applicable residency requirements for the role, and have the right to work in the United Kingdom. Some roles may also be subject to nationality requirements where these are necessary to meet UK Government or contractual security obligations.**

**The role is based on-site in Hampshire 5 days a week.**

Role Summary

The Technical Security Architect is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining technical security architectures that protect the organisation's information systems, data, and infrastructure. Embedded within the Technical team, this role leads the tech refresh and evergreening of security toolsets - ensuring the security technology estate remains current, supported, effective, and aligned with evolving threat landscapes, client policies, and cross-domain architectural patterns.

The Technical Security Architect is expected to produce detailed technical designs, evaluate and select security technologies, define integration patterns, and guide implementation teams through delivery. The role requires deep technical expertise across cloud security, identity and access management, boundary and perimeter security, secure platform architectures, and security tooling ecosystems.

Key Responsibilities

Security Architecture Design & Development

* Design and develop technical security architectures for new and existing services, platforms, and infrastructure

* Produce detailed security architecture documentation including High-Level Designs (HLDs), Low-Level Designs (LLDs), security patterns, data flow diagrams, and integration specifications.

* Define security architecture principles, standards, and patterns that guide technology decisions across the organisation.

* Ensure security architectures address the full security stack: identity, authentication, authorisation, encryption, network segmentation, boundary protection, endpoint security, logging, monitoring, and incident detection.

Security Toolset Tech Refresh & Evergreening

* Lead the technical planning, design, and architecture for the refresh and evergreening of the security toolset estate

* Develop tech refresh roadmaps for security toolsets - prioritised by risk exposure, vendor support status, capability gaps, and strategic alignment.

* Evaluate, assess, and recommend security technologies through structured evaluation processes including proof of concept (PoC), proof of value (PoV), and technical benchmarking.

Cross-Domain Architecture & Pattern Alignment

* Ensure security architectures align with and contribute to cross-domain architectural patterns - including infrastructure, network, platform, application, and data architecture.

* Define reusable security architecture patterns and reference architectures that can be applied consistently across projects and services.

* Collaborate with enterprise architects, infrastructure architects, network architects, and application architects to ensure security is embedded in all architectural decisions - not bolted on.

Cloud Security Architecture

* Design security architectures for public cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP), private cloud, hybrid cloud, and multi-cloud environments.

* Define cloud security reference architectures

Identity & Access Management Architecture

* Design and maintain IAM architectures

* Ensure IAM architectures support operational requirements including break-glass procedures, emergency access, and audit trail integrity.

Boundary & Network Security Architecture

* Design boundary and network security architectures

* Ensure boundary security designs support both traditional perimeter models and Zero Trust Network Architecture (ZTNA) principles.

Secure Platform Architecture

* Design security controls and hardening standards for platform architectures

* Define secure build standards, hardening baselines (CIS Benchmarks, DISA STIGs), and compliance validation approaches.

Risk Management & Threat-Informed Design

* Apply threat modelling methodologies (e.g., STRIDE, MITRE ATT&CK, kill chain analysis) to inform security architecture decisions.

* Identify, assess, and document security risks associated with architectural designs, technology choices, and toolset transitions.

* Maintain a security architecture risk register and ensure risks are communicated to stakeholders with clear mitigation recommendations.

Required Skills & Experience

Essential

* Significant experience in a Technical Security Architect or Senior Security Engineer role, designing and delivering security architectures in complex enterprise environments.

* **TOGAF and/or SABSA certification**

* **CISSP certification (or equivalent)**

* Deep technical expertise across multiple security domains: identity & access management, boundary/perimeter security, cloud security, endpoint security, network security, and secure platform architectures.

* Proven experience leading security toolset refresh, migration, and evergreening programmes.

* Strong experience designing security architectures for cloud environments (AWS, Azure, and/or GCP).

Jointly with the Team Director, and Regional Heads the Head will co-lead the Bank’s engagement with large clients, Government authorities and other internal and external stakeholders including country management and Policy teams contributing to setting the Team’s strategy. **Background**

Telecommunications, Media and Technology is at the core of EBRD activities. EBRD aims to maximize the potential of companies in all countries it operates in by addressing their specific needs through tailored financing. Total investments in TMT account for EUR 500-600m annually in over 20 projects across EBRD’s countries of operations.

The team comprises 20 full-time professionals and works with a large number of colleagues in the EBRD Resident Offices.

Represent the TMT Team in the Bank's management approval forums and the Board, in relation to the relevant projects, issues and initiatives as required. Extensive travel to meet counterparts and stakeholders.
* **Champion and role model** the Bank’s Workplace Behaviours and Competencies, ensuring adherence within the Team so that the highest standards of integrity and ethical conduct are exhibited at all times.
* **General:**Carry out other relevant tasks assigned by Team Director; take leadership on specific initiatives.

* Previous experience in origination and execution of a significant number of complex deals.

## Job Description

**Could you be the technical expert who shapes how our solar and battery storage projects connect to the grid, guiding critical engineering decisions from early feasibility through to energisation?**   
We're looking for a Senior HV Engineer to join our Elgin's Engineering team as the in-house technical authority for grid connection and HV engineering across our utility-scale solar PV and co-located BESS projects in the UK and Ireland, with the potential to support Elgin's projects in Italy. The role follows the project lifecycle: grid feasibility and connection optioneering, development-stage engineering to support consents, land and grid applications, technical specification for procurement, and technical assurance of the contractors' design, construction and energisation. Elgin does not carry out detailed design in-house; detailed design and construction are delivered by ICP, iDNO and EPC contractors against Elgin's Employer's Requirements.  
   
   
The focus of the role is engineering and de-risking from the earliest stage of a project: bringing the grid engineering into development so that the connection method, cable route and substation requirements are settled through the feasibility work, planning applications, land agreements and grid applications rather than discovered later; making sure each connection is technically deliverable and that the contestable / non-contestable scope split is right before it is fixed in budgets and contracts; and assuring that the designs produced by ICPs, iDNOs and consultants meet Elgin's Employer's Requirements and the network operator's standards. Commercial and programme management of the DNO / TSO relationship sits outside of this role; this role provides the engineering judgement behind it.  
   
   
Elgin does not design or build its projects itself: it sets the technical requirements and its contractors deliver against them. The value of this role is in setting those requirements well and in challenging what consultants and contractors deliver. You will be the technical escalation and decision on HV and grid matters and the primary technical contact for Elgin's development-stage consultants and ICPs.

**What you will do:**  
  
**Development stage**  

* Lead the technical side of connection method and grid route optioneering for Development: scope and direct the feasibility studies, judge overhead line, underground cable and hybrid options on constructability, consentability, land take and cost, and recommend the option to take forward.
* Get the grid engineering into the development case early, so that it is reflected in consents and land rather than discovered at procurement: define the substation footprint, cable route corridor and crossing strategy for planning applications and consents, provide the technical input to land, wayleave and easement discussions, and prepare the technical inputs to grid connection and modification applications (DNO / NESO in GB, ESB Networks / EirGrid in Ireland).
* Produce concept-level single line diagrams, substation layouts and route corridors with the CAD team, to the level needed for feasibility, planning and tender purposes only; detailed design sits with the ICP, iDNO and EPC contractors. Discharge Elgin's CDM 2015 designer duties for the concept designs it produces.
* Act as primary technical contact for Elgin's development-stage consultants on cable routes, HV design and power system studies: define technical scopes, review deliverables and challenge conclusions before they enter project decisions. This is development-stage consultancy; detailed design is delivered by the EPC and ICP contractors.
* Specify and review the cable modelling, ampacity and losses studies (MV through 132 kV, and 220 kV in Ireland) carried out by consultants and contractors, and make sure the results feed the design basis, CAPEX and energy yield assumptions.
* Set and challenge the technical grid CAPEX assumptions and the engineering basis of the connection programme as they enter the investment case, and produce the technical reports, planning inputs and position papers that stand up to Investment Committee and lender scrutiny.

  
**Grid connection**  

* Technically interpret connection offers, Connection Agreements and technical schedules, on Elgin's own projects and in acquisition due diligence: what they commit Elgin to, where the contestable / non-contestable boundary sits, and the omissions, abnormal costs and onerous conditions behind them.
* Review and challenge network study outputs (fault level, harmonics, reactive capability, protection) and turn them into Employer's Requirements and contestable / non-contestable scope decisions for the ICP and EPC turnkey contracts.
* Own the contestable / non-contestable / Contractor interface on each project: define and record the scope split and close gaps and duplication between DNO, iDNO, ICP and EPC scopes before they become variations.
* Ensure the G99 / Grid Code compliance obligations in the Connection Agreement are allocated between the ICP and EPC scopes in the ERs and DoR, and own Elgin's technical compliance position with the network operator as the connection customer; lead any derogation application on Elgin's behalf, and witness compliance testing where required.

**Procurement and contracts support**  

* Author and maintain the HV and grid sections of Elgin's Employer's Requirements and Division of Responsibilities matrix, and support Procurement through ICP, iDNO and EPC tendering, evaluation and technical negotiation.

  
**Construction, commissioning and energisation (assurance and escalation)**  

* Assure the contractors' HV and grid design rather than produce it: make sure ICP, iDNO and EPC design submissions are reviewed against Elgin's Employer's Requirements and the network operator's standards (through the Owner's Engineer where one is appointed), decide Elgin's position on deviations with a reasoned justification, and close out Owner's Engineer comments.
* Act as Elgin's technical escalation point for the Project Engineers, the Owner's Engineer and the PMA through construction, commissioning and energisation: decide Elgin's response where site works deviate from design intent or the Connection Agreement, review the contractors' Grid Code compliance and energisation submissions before they go to the network operator, and attend key witness tests. Day-to-day technical queries and routine witnessing sit with the Owner's Engineer and the contractors.

  
**Ongoing**  

* Maintain Elgin's HV and grid engineering standards, templates and lessons learned, keep abreast of DNO / TSO standards and policy change.

## Your profile

* BEng / MEng in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems or a related discipline.
* Extensive HV and grid connection engineering experience (MV through 132 kV), including delivered UK utility-scale solar, BESS or ICP / DNO connection projects through to energisation.
* Detailed working knowledge of the GB connection process: G99, Connection Agreements and technical schedules, contestable and non-contestable works, the ICP and iDNO model, DNO design approval and adoption, and derogations.
* Experience of development-stage grid work: connection and modification applications, connection offer assessment, connection method and route optioneering, and technical inputs to planning applications and land agreements.
* Ability to read and challenge network study outputs and translate them into design and scope decisions.
* Strong HV design review capability: switchgear and protection, earthing, HV cables and routes, HDD and crossings, substations and transformers, metering, auxiliary supplies, SCADA / telecoms.
* Experience authoring or reviewing Employer's Requirements and Division of Responsibilities under EPC and ICP contracts, and scoping and challenging external consultants.
* Ability to translate technical decisions into CAPEX, programme and risk implications and communicate them clearly, in writing and in person, to non-technical stakeholders.
* Ability to specify, review and challenge cable modelling, ampacity and losses studies and power system studies, with working familiarity with AutoCAD and power system analysis tools.
* Full driving licence and willingness to travel to project sites in the UK and Ireland as required.

**Desirable**  

* Chartered Engineer (CEng) or working towards chartership.
* Irish connection experience (ESB Networks / EirGrid, CRU policy, ECP and RESS delivery) and transmission-level (110 kV to 220 kV) experience.
* BESS and co-located hybrid connections, including Grid Code compliance for storage.
* Power system modelling (DIgSILENT PowerFactory, ETAP or PSCAD); technical due diligence for acquisitions or lenders; CDM 2015 designer duties.
* Experience across multiple network operators (NGED, UKPN, SPEN, NPg, SSEN) and National Grid / NESO.
* Exposure to the Italian connection process (Terna and the distribution operators) for solar or BESS projects.

Contact centre architecture more broadly. Agent Copilot and Cisco Finesse integration. SSML and advanced TTS tuning. SIP, WebRTC, Twilio or similar. CRM, case management or CCaaS integrations. # Technical Product Owner

## 🚀 Ready to build what’s next? We’re looking for a Technical Product Owner to help shape the future of Eque2 Estimating and AI-powered product innovation.🚀

**Who are Eque2?**

Eque2 provides specialist software for the construction and housebuilding sectors, helping businesses manage everything from estimating and financial management to commercial operations and project delivery.

We work with leading platforms including Microsoft, Sage and Xero, helping construction businesses improve visibility, stay in control and manage their operations more effectively. Today, we support over 3,000 construction businesses across the UK and Ireland, from growing contractors to large, complex organisations.

**Role Purpose**

To own and prioritise the delivery backlog for Eque2’s cloud estimating and cost-control product, translating product direction and validated customer needs into delivery-ready work. You will use AI-enabled development, design and product management tools to accelerate delivery and help build market-leading customer-facing Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities.

**About the Role**

We are seeking a Technical Product Owner to help shape the next generation of Eque2’s cloud estimating and cost-control software. Reporting to the Chalkstring Product Director, you will own backlog quality, prioritisation and day-to-day delivery decisions within the direction set by Product Management, defining clear requirements and testable acceptance criteria for Engineering and QA.

You will partner with Product Management, Product Design, Engineering and QA from discovery and rapid prototyping through to customer delivery and validation. You will use AI-enabled product, design and development tools to accelerate this process and play a central role in expanding Chalkstring with capabilities from our established EValuate product.

You will engage directly with customers to understand their processes, validate use cases, explore emerging AI opportunities and support acceptance testing, using customer and delivery evidence to inform product decisions.

**Location:** This is a UK-based hybrid role, with office access in Maidenhead and Newcastle-upon-Tyne. Travel is required for team, customer and stakeholder meetings, with office attendance expected 1–2 days per week.

**Is this role right for you?**

This is a hands-on product delivery role rather than a Product Management position.

You will have authority over the delivery backlog, priorities and day-to-day delivery decisions within the direction set by Product Management. Product Management retains ownership of overall product strategy, roadmap direction, pricing and market positioning.

This role will suit someone who enjoys being close to customers, Engineering and delivery, and who can turn broad product direction and complex customer needs into well-defined work that teams can confidently build and test.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Own and prioritise the delivery backlog within Product Management’s agreed direction, making trade-offs, dependencies and delivery decisions visible.
* Turn validated customer needs into delivery-ready epics, stories, workflows and acceptance criteria that Engineering and QA can implement and test without repeated clarification.
* Lead refinement and contribute actively to sprint planning and reviews, resolving ambiguity quickly and accepting completed work against agreed criteria.
* Engage directly with construction customers to understand estimating and cost-control workflows, validate use cases and edge cases, and support user acceptance and adoption.
* Use AI-enabled development, design and product management tools to accelerate research, requirements, prototyping and delivery while maintaining appropriate review, security and data controls.
* Identify and validate valuable customer-facing AI opportunities, defining quality thresholds, safeguards, human oversight and evaluation requirements for probabilistic features.
* Work closely with Product Design, Engineering and QA on workflows, data models, integrations, APIs, technical constraints and testability.
* Measure adoption, quality and customer outcomes; use evidence to guide iteration, priorities and recommendations to Product Management.
* Communicate progress, decisions, risks and dependencies clearly, and keep product documentation, release notes, Support and Customer Success briefings current.

**Knowledge, Skills & Experience**

* Demonstrable experience as a Product Owner, Business Analyst or in a closely related B2B SaaS delivery role.
* Practical experience owning and prioritising backlogs within an Agile delivery environment.
* A strong track record of translating customer and operational needs into clear user stories, requirements and testable acceptance criteria.
* Strong process, workflow and data analysis skills.
* Enough technical understanding to discuss APIs, integrations, data and dependencies confidently with Engineering teams.
* Hands-on experience using AI tools in areas such as product discovery, analysis, design, requirements or prototyping.
* An understanding of the quality, risk and human-oversight considerations associated with customer-facing AI.
* Confidence engaging directly with customers and communicating technical and product decisions to different audiences.
* An evidence-led, proactive and collaborative approach, with strong attention to detail.
* Experience using Jira or a comparable product delivery tool.

**Desirable**

* Construction estimating, quantity surveying or cost control.
* EValuate or other construction estimating software.
* AI, machine-learning or data-driven product capabilities within complex B2B workflows.
* AI prototyping, evaluation or observability tools.
* Low-code or no-code platforms or AI coding assistants.
* SQL.
* API tools such as Postman or Swagger.
* Process modelling, including BPMN.

**Personal attributes**

You are a practical, customer-focused Product Owner who enjoys turning complex operational problems into clear, deliverable outcomes.

You are comfortable getting into the detail with engineers while keeping sight of the customer problem and intended outcome. You ask precise questions, challenge assumptions and identify dependencies early rather than allowing ambiguity to reach Engineering.

You will be:

* **Curious and evidence-led**, using customer and delivery insight to inform decisions.
* **Proactive and solutions-focused**, comfortable resolving ambiguity and moving work forward.
* **Commercially and technically credible**, able to communicate confidently with customers, engineers and senior stakeholders.
* **Collaborative and adaptable**, working effectively across Product Management, Product Design, Engineering and QA.
* **Quality-conscious**, balancing pace and innovation with security, responsible AI use and customer trust.

**The successful candidate will be:**

* Highly organised, detail-oriented and effective at managing time and priorities.
* Professional, credible and confident when engaging with senior stakeholders.
* Proactive, solutions-focused and able to anticipate needs.
* Calm under pressure and adaptable to changing priorities.
* Trustworthy, discreet and demonstrates sound judgement.
* Collaborative, approachable and service oriented.
* A positive ambassador for the organisation’s culture, values and standards.

**Measures of Success**

**Success in this role will be demonstrated through:**

* **Backlog readiness:** priority work has a clear outcome, scope, acceptance criteria and dependencies before it reaches sprint planning.
* **Requirement quality:** Engineering and QA can implement and test work without recurring clarification, with requirement-related rework reduced over time.
* **Delivery predictability:** risks, dependencies and material scope changes are identified and communicated early.
* **Customer validation:** priority features are tested with representative customers and validated against defined needs and use cases.
* **AI quality and safety:** customer-facing AI capabilities meet agreed standards for quality, reliability, privacy, security and appropriate human oversight before release.
* **Adoption and value:** released capabilities have clear outcome measures, such as adoption, usage, satisfaction or operational improvement, which are reviewed after launch.
* **AI-enabled productivity:** AI tools demonstrably improve discovery, prototyping or delivery without weakening quality, controls or traceability.
* **Operational readiness:** relevant documentation, release notes and Support and Customer Success briefings are complete before launch.

We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer, committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued, respected and has the opportunity to thrive.

Director, Microsoft AI & Data Solution Architect
The opportunity
We are looking for an experienced Microsoft AI & Data Solution Architect at Director level to help shape and deliver complex AI and data transformation programmes for our clients.
The role combines pre-sales solution architecture with senior delivery leadership. You will work with senior business and technology stakeholders to understand their ambitions, shape compelling Microsoft-based solutions and translate those solutions into secure, scalable and deliverable architectures.
You will bring the technical depth to engage credibly with enterprise and solution architects, while also having the consulting experience to lead client conversations, support complex pursuits and take senior accountability for delivery.
This is a client-facing consulting role for someone who can operate comfortably from early opportunity shaping and RFP response through to architecture, mobilisation and delivery.
Your key responsibilities
Solution architecture and pre-sales

Lead the architecture and solution shaping of complex Microsoft AI & Data opportunities, translating client objectives into pragmatic, scalable and value-led solutions.
Facilitate architecture and solution workshops with senior business and technology stakeholders.
Develop end-to-end solution architectures spanning data platforms, analytics, AI, agentic AI, security, governance and integration.
Provide technical leadership for proposals, RFP responses, statements of work and other pursuit activities, ensuring proposed solutions are ambitious but also credible and deliverable.
Work with delivery and commercial teams to develop solution estimates, delivery approaches, assumptions, dependencies and technical scope.
Communicate complex architectural concepts clearly to a range of audiences, from senior executives through to client architects and engineering teams.
Lead or oversee the development of demonstrations and proofs of concept where these help clients understand the art of the possible.

Client delivery and architecture leadership

Act as a senior engagement lead and/or senior architect on significant Microsoft AI & Data programmes.
Provide architectural direction and technical assurance across the delivery lifecycle.
Work closely with client enterprise and solution architects, providing credible challenge and resolving complex architectural decisions.
Ensure solutions appropriately address security, governance, resilience, operability, performance and other non-functional requirements.
Maintain continuity between what EY sells and what EY delivers, ensuring architectural commitments made during pursuits translate effectively into delivery.
Lead multidisciplinary teams of architects, engineers, data specialists and other consultants, providing technical direction, coaching and quality oversight.

Skills and attributes for success
We are looking for someone who combines strong architecture credentials with substantial consulting and client-facing experience.
You should have:

Significant experience designing enterprise-scale AI, data and analytics solutions using Microsoft technologies.
Strong solution architecture skills and the technical credibility to lead architecture discussions with senior client architects and engineering leaders.
Deep understanding of modern data platform architecture, including data engineering, integration, modelling, analytics, governance and AI.
Strong understanding of enterprise generative AI and agentic AI architectures, including the considerations required to move solutions from experimentation into secure, governed and scalable production environments.
Experience operating within a consulting or professional services environment and working directly with senior client stakeholders.
Demonstrable experience supporting sales and pre-sales activity, including proposals, RFPs, solution shaping, estimation and statements of work.
Experience leading complex client engagements as a senior engagement leader and/or senior solution architect.
Ability to balance technical ambition with practical considerations including business value, delivery risk, security, governance, cost and operability.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience leading and developing architects and engineers within multidisciplinary delivery teams.

Microsoft technology experience
Candidates should bring strong experience across a number of the following:

Microsoft Fabric
Azure AI Foundry
Azure OpenAI and Azure AI services
Microsoft agent technologies
Microsoft Purview
Azure data services
Power BI and semantic modelling
Azure cloud architecture, security and identity
APIs, integration and cloud-native architecture
DevOps, CI/CD and production engineering practices

Experience of Databricks and/or Snowflake in enterprise data architectures would be advantageous.
Hands-on engineering is not the primary purpose of the role, but the ability to prototype, lead the creation of demonstrations or work directly with technology where appropriate would be beneficial.
What we look for
A successful candidate is likely to be someone who can move naturally between three quite different conversations:



With a CIO or CDO:What business outcome are we seeking, what architectural choices matter and how does the investment create value?
With an Enterprise Architect:How does the solution fit the existing technology estate, and how will data, AI, security, identity, governance and integration work end to end?
With an EY delivery team:What exactly are we building, what are the key architecture decisions and risks, and how do we deliver it successfully?



That combination is important. This isn't a pure sales role, a pure engineering role or a conventional programme leadership role. It needs someone with enough technical depth to be recognised as an architect, coupled with the consulting maturity to shape opportunities and then take senior responsibility for what is delivered.
Location and working arrangements
The position would be a permanent UK Director role, aligned to EY's main UK offices, with travel to client sites as required.

# The FT World Desk Fellowship

United Kingdom

**About us**

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

*Build a newsworthy career at the FT.*

**Our commitment to inclusion and fairness**

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

**The Financial Times has an exciting opportunity for aspiring Black foreign correspondents.**

Are you keen to report on the world at this time of tumult? Are you excited by international news and do you want a hand in interpreting and explaining it to a global audience? Are you tempted by the idea of a wide-ranging career in journalism reporting on dramatic events from across the globe? If so, then our new six-month World Desk fellowship would suit you well.   

The FT’s global, award-winning editorial team represents the gold standard in journalism, seeking depth, originality and balance that differentiates the FT from the pack and engages subscribers.

The Fellowship is a six-month, paid fellowship in the heart of the FT’s London newsroom. You will join the World News Desk, where a dozen-strong team of accomplished journalists commission and edit our global coverage.   

You will work with the editors to help deliver ground-breaking coverage. You will also work closely with our London-based regional editors, the Africa Editor, Europe Editor, Latin America Editor and Middle East Editor, helping them with their coverage.

You will support the global network of correspondents with research and ideas for how to complement their stories with the right data and visual elements. You will be encouraged to write your own stories and will have mentoring from senior FT editors, in particular the foreign editor, in how to conceive and craft an “FT story”.

**What You Will Learn**

You will be part of a team of experienced journalists covering the world, and there may also be opportunities for short-term stints on other editorial desks. You will learn the timeless arts of writing clear crisp copy and reporting on complex and sensitive stories. 

You will also gain insight into the essential skills of cutting-edge digital journalism and story-telling. The overarching ambition of the fellowship is to help to equip you one day to be a foreign correspondent, hopefully for the FT.

**Knowledge, Skills and Experience**

The successful candidate will:

* Display a keen interest in international affairs
* Want to pursue a career in journalism covering global news
* Be capable of keeping a cool head under deadline pressure
* Care deeply about writing accurately and objectively

Some experience in journalism is preferable but not essential. Career change applications are also welcome.

This opportunity is designed for Black candidates to help to address historical under-representation in the media, and to support greater diversity.

**How to apply**

All applicants must have the right to work in the United Kingdom.

Please upload **three documents**:

* **CV**
* **A Cover Letter detailing what you will bring to the role and why you think you are suitable**
* **An unpublished article on an international story (600 words max)**

The deadline for applications is 8pm on Sunday 15th November 2026.

**Further information**

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview and to take a short writing test. The successful applicant will join the World News Desk and report to the FT’s Foreign Editor, Alec Russell.  

This 6-month fellowship is for 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday, starting in Spring 2027.

The fellow will receive a monthly bursary of £2,500.

**The use of AI**

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism.  Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

**Accessibility**

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

Focal Systems is the industry leader in retail AI solutions. We are headquartered in San Francisco, California with operations in Canada and the UK, and a tech-hub in Poland. We are a Deep Learning first company. Our mission is to automate and optimize brick and mortar retail using deep learning computer vision. Focal Systems has been deployed at scale with some of the top retailers in the world.

## **About the Role**

As Supply Chain Coordinator, you will keep our camera hardware moving across the UK. You will coordinate the day-to-day supply chain, from inbound shipments and stock control through warehousing, outbound deliveries to field teams, and the returns and repair loop that gets equipment back into service.

Our UK operations run in cycles, with periods of rapid scale-up for new retailer rollouts followed by quieter maintenance periods. You will help make sure the right hardware is in the right place at the right time through each of those shifts, keeping stock levels and deliveries in step with the deployment schedule.  
  
You will track and run day-to-day activity at our warehouse and storage locations across the UK, coordinate with field teams, couriers, and our supply chain team, and be the go-to person for an accurate picture of UK stock and logistics.

* You are organised and proactive, and you enjoy keeping lots of moving parts on track

* Track stock levels against the deployment schedule and flag shortages or surpluses early, helping us prepare for scale-up and scale-down periods
* Book and track inbound shipments from our global supply chain, including supporting with the preparation of import and customs paperwork and liaising with suppliers
