Our values reflect us all and they’re at the heart of everything we do. They set out our culture, the way we behave and the way we do things.

\*  We are looking for a passionate and knowledgeable Behaviour Analyst to help us bring our positive support model, Strive, to life across our services.

\*          Strive is at the heart of how we deliver active care and support. It’s about being proactive, not reactive — understanding individual needs, planning and creating the right environments for people to develop skills, build independence and enjoy greater choice and control over their lives.

\*          If you’re passionate about Positive Behaviour Support (PBS), committed to evidence-based practice and motivated by helping people achieve their personal goals, this is an opportunity to make a genuine difference.

**Key Responsibilities:**

As a Behaviour Analyst, you will play an important role in embedding Strive across our services, working alongside our PBS Practitioners, operational colleagues and multidisciplinary teams to ensure the people we support receive high-quality, person-centred care.

You will use your specialist knowledge to influence practice, build confidence within our teams and ensure our approach focuses on understanding the person, promoting positive outcomes and reducing the need for restrictive practices.

Your responsibilities will include:

* Championing Strive: Supporting the implementation of our positive support model across services and ensuring proactive, person-centred approaches are embedded in everyday practice.
* Developing effective PBS plans: Designing and supporting the implementation of evidence-based Positive Behaviour Support plans and interventions that increase skills, promote independence and reduce behaviours of concern.
* Supporting our PBS Practitioners: Providing guidance, supervision and coaching to help our practitioners develop their knowledge, confidence and professional practice.
* Delivering training and development: Facilitating Active Support and PBS training, evaluating its impact and ensuring learning translates into improved practice and better outcomes.
* Driving positive change: Working in partnership with Regional Leadership Teams to improve the experiences of the people we support and our colleagues.
* Reducing restrictive practices: Working collaboratively with services to identify proactive alternatives, promote dignity and choice, and support people to live more fulfilling lives.
* Promoting best practice: Applying evidence-based approaches that enable people to achieve their person-centred goals and make meaningful progress.
* Building effective partnerships: Working with multidisciplinary teams and a range of stakeholders, bringing different perspectives together to achieve the best possible outcomes.

**Key Skills and Experience:**

You will be a confident and compassionate Behaviour Analyst who can combine technical expertise with a practical, collaborative approach. You’ll be comfortable supporting colleagues, influencing practice and helping teams understand how the right support can transform someone’s everyday experience.

**Essential**

-        A Master’s degree in Applied Behaviour Analysis or Positive Behaviour Support.

-        BCBA or UKBA(cert) certification.

-        Registration with UK-SBA, or a willingness to register.

-        At least one year’s experience working within social care.

-        Demonstrable experience developing and implementing Positive Behaviour Support plans and interventions to build skills and reduce behaviours of concern.

-        Experience working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and balancing differing stakeholder views.

-        Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence, coach and support others.

-        A commitment to person-centred practice, evidence-based interventions and the reduction of restrictive practices.

Above all, you will share our belief that behaviour is meaningful, that understanding the individual is fundamental to effective support, and that everyone deserves the opportunity to thrive.

\*          We’re looking for an experienced and passionate Positive Behaviour Support (PBS) Practitioner to join our PBS team, reporting to the Lead Behaviour Analyst. This is an opportunity to use your specialist clinical knowledge, influence practice across our services and help create lasting, positive change for the people we support.

\*          You will be passionate about person-centred practice, reducing restrictive interventions and empowering colleagues to deliver outstanding support.

**Key Responsibilities:**

You will play a key role in embedding our PBS approach across the region, working closely with the people we support, operational teams, families and internal and external multidisciplinary teams.

Your focus will be on improving quality of life through proactive, evidence-informed and person-centred interventions that help people develop skills, build independence and achieve their aspirations.

Your responsibilities will include:

* Developing effective PBS interventions: Assess individual needs, develop function-based PBS plans and skill-building programmes, and support colleagues to implement them consistently and effectively.
* Championing co-production: Involve people with lived experience in their PBS assessments, plans and reviews, ensuring their voices, preferences and aspirations shape the support they receive.
* Driving positive change: Support ivolve’s group-wide strategy to reduce restrictive practices, using data and evidence to inform meaningful and sustainable improvements.
* Developing confident teams: Deliver person-specific PBS training, Tier 1 interventions and practice leadership training, equipping colleagues with the knowledge and confidence to provide the best possible support.
* Measuring what matters: Collect and analyse person-centred data, monitor behavioural trends, undertake audits and reviews, and communicate findings to inform clinical practice and improve outcomes.
* Supporting new services: Contribute to pre-admission assessments, transitions and referrals, helping us understand individual needs and plan the right support from the outset.
* Strengthening clinical partnerships: Work collaboratively with internal and external multidisciplinary teams, families and operational colleagues to overcome barriers, share expertise and embed best practice.
* Promoting reflective practice: Facilitate debriefs, encourage learning and reflection, and support colleagues to continuously develop their practice.
* Contributing to service improvement: Support clinical pathways, working groups and organisational initiatives, ensuring our PBS approach continues to evolve and deliver great standards.

You will also work closely with the Lead Behaviour Analyst, contribute to monthly performance updates and take part in regular clinical supervision and continuing professional development.

**Key Skills and Experience:**

You’ll be a confident, values-led practitioner who combines specialist clinical knowledge with the ability to influence, inspire and support others. You’ll understand that successful PBS is about much more than plans and interventions; it’s about understanding people, building relationships and creating environments where individuals can thrive.

**Essential**

-        BTEC Diploma Level 5 Positive Behaviour Support (PBS).

-        Willingness to register UK Society for Behaviour Analysis (UK-SBA), an organisation accredited by the Professional Standards Authority (PSA).

-        Experience delivering highly specialist PBS interventions within a PBS-informed service.

-        Knowledge of trauma-informed care and restrictive practice reduction.

-        Evidence of ongoing continuing professional development (CPD).

-        Strong analytical skills, with the ability to collect, interpret and communicate data to demonstrate individual and organisational outcomes.

-        Experience implementing organisational strategy and supporting change at scale.

-        Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the resilience, creativity and interpersonal skills to engage teams and influence positive practice.

-        The ability to travel effectively across ivolve services.

-        A willingness to develop further specialist expertise, for example in mental health.

**Desirable**

-        UK-SBA certification, Behaviour Analyst Certification Board (BACB) certification, or working towards certification.

-        Membership of relevant professional special interest groups.

-        Experience of research, clinical audits or service evaluation.

-        Previous experience working within a multidisciplinary team.

**If you’re ready for a job that can truly make a difference and you’re up for a challenge, then this is the role for you!**

**The team**

The Compliance team’s mission is to keep iwoca a safe and trusted lender for UK small businesses, and to make the compliant path the easy path for the teams we work with.

We make sure iwoca meets its regulatory obligations, particularly the financial crime, sanctions and data protection requirements that apply across our suite of products and services.

We are the second line of defence for the UK business. We advise the people building and running the business on what the rules require, set the policies and standards they work to, and test whether what happens in practice matches them. We work alongside the product teams so that each product meets its obligations and can grow.

Data protection is central to what we do. We hold the data privacy function for the UK business and own how iwoca handles personal data end to end: the lawful basis for how customer, applicant and third-party data is used; data subject access requests and other individual rights; personal data breaches; retention and deletion; records of processing; marketing and consent; the privacy review of new products and features; and the governance of automated decisioning and AI tooling.

***How we work:***

* We enable rather than block. The answer is rarely just “no” — it’s what it would take to get to yes, and what the firm is accepting if it goes ahead anyway.
* We go to the source. Positions are grounded in the actual rule, regulation or guidance, and we can show where they come from.
* We’re proportionate. Controls match the risk in front of us. We don’t build process for its own sake.
* We’re close to the business. We work directly with Tech, Data, Credit, Operations and Legal, and we want to be in the room early rather than at the end.

**The role**

As Data Privacy Analyst you will run iwoca’s day-to-day UK data protection work and help the business apply UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR in practice. Your primary focus will be the statutory core: data subject access requests, data protection impact assessments, legitimate interests assessments, personal data breaches and records of processing.

The role is not only to run that work but to improve it. A significant part of the job is identifying where our privacy operations could be automated, supported by AI or otherwise improved, assessing what each option would take and what it would mean for compliance, and specifying it well enough for our Tech and Data teams to deliver.

There is real room for the role to grow: as you build credibility, so does the scope, towards owning areas of the framework outright, leading on AI and automation governance, and taking a larger advisory remit across the business.

You will report to the Data Privacy Manager and work closely with the Head of Compliance who also acts as iwoca’s DPO, so you will have experienced support on the harder judgement calls. This is a hands-on role and the work is visible — much of it goes to senior stakeholders or to the regulator.

***Impact and influence***

* Individual rights and data breaches. Own data subject access requests from intake to response — scoping the search, applying exemptions and meeting the statutory deadline — along with erasure, rectification and objection requests. Triage and investigate suspected personal data breaches, assess them against the 72-hour notification test, and keep the breach register accurate.
* Privacy assessments and advice. Assist with DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments and other privacy reviews on new products, features, suppliers and data flows. Be an accessible first point of contact for teams across iwoca with a data protection question, and give them an answer they can act on, early enough to shape what they build.
* Records, policies and reporting. Keep the record of processing activities accurate as the business changes, hold the retention and deletion schedules to account, review data processing agreements with suppliers, help maintain our data protection policies and standards, and produce the privacy reporting that goes to senior stakeholders.
* AI and automated decisioning. Help assess AI tooling and automated decision-making across lending and operations: what personal data goes in, what lawful basis supports it, what the model does with it, and what rights customers have over the outcome. That includes the risks specific to these systems — decisions taken without meaningful human involvement, bias in outcomes, unreliable model output — and recommending how we address them.
* Automation and improvement. Identify the manual steps in our privacy operations that should not be manual, assess the options, and set out the requirements and compliance implications clearly enough for Tech and Data to deliver them.

**The requirements**

* Experience. Experience in data protection or privacy operations, or in a compliance, legal, risk or operational role where data protection was a real part of the job.

* Privacy operations and assessments. Hands-on experience of statutory work: DSARs, DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments, breach handling, ROPA maintenance or data processing agreement review. You may not have done all of these — but we want to see that you have done some of them properly.
* AI and automation. A real interest in, and working understanding of, how data protection law applies to AI and automated decision-making. Enough technical fluency to see where a manual process could be automated, set out what is needed, and hold your own in a conversation with engineers.
* Stakeholder management: Comfortable dealing directly with product, engineering, marketing, credit and operations teams, and able to give a non-specialist a clear answer they can act on rather than a legal summary.

**Bonus:**

* Sector experience. Financial services or fintech, ideally in lending or payments.

* Practical tooling. Experience using Claude Code, LLMs or privacy management platforms.

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent Kernel ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at **Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Notion** already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

The Data Privacy Manager (“Privacy Manager”) is responsible for managing,
co-ordinating and generally implementing KLDiscovery’s data protection strategy
and ensuring compliance with applicable data protection laws, including the
General Data Protection Regulation (“GDPR”), the UK Data Protection Act 2018 and
US State privacy laws including the California Consumer Privacy Act (“CCPA”) and
Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (“HIPAA”). The Privacy
Manager will act as the internal lead for KLDiscovery on data privacy queries,
serves as the primary point of contact for data subjects and regulatory
authorities, provides expert advice on data protection matters, undertakes
implementation of data privacy initiatives, ensures compliance with KLDiscovery
policies and supports KLDiscovery in managing risks associated with the
processing of personal data for clients and employees.

 

 

Key Responsibilities

Compliance Monitoring and Advisory

 * Monitor compliance against global data protection laws and internal policies,
   procedures, and controls, both for clients and employees.
 * Advise KLDiscovery and its employees on data protection obligations and best
   practices.
 * Monitor emerging trends, legislative changes, and guidance relating to data
   privacy, particularly involving use of artificial-intelligence.

 

Risk and Assessment

 * Conduct regular audits, risk assessments, and reviews of data processing
   activities including vendor due diligence as it relates Data Privacy
   Assessments.
 * Co-ordinate and manage Data Protection Impact Assessments (“DPIAs”), Transfer
   Impact Assessments (“TIAs”), Legitimate Interest Assessments (‘’LIAs’’) and
   advise on mitigating risks for both product and internal initiatives.
 * Maintain KLDiscovery’s compliance with cross‑border data transfer
   requirements, including the Data Privacy Framework (“DPF”), Schrems II
   obligations, and any successor or equivalent transfer mechanisms.

 

Records and Documentation

 * Own and maintain the Records of Processing Activities (“ROPA”) as required by
   law on a per country basis, covering all business units.
 * Develop and maintain data protection policies, privacy notices, and
   supporting documentation.
 * Assist in development of contractual frameworks for clients and providing
   advice on best practices.

 

Data Subject and Regulatory Liaison

 * Serve as the primary contact for data subjects regarding data protection
   queries, complaints, and requests, including Subject Access Requests
   (“SARs”), with responses managed within applicable statutory timeframes and
   data deletion.
 * Act as the primary liaison with supervisory authorities and facilitate
   communication in the event of a data breach or investigation.
 * Support the cybersecurity incident response process by providing expert
   guidance on breach classification, notification obligations, and regulatory
   reporting requirements across applicable jurisdictions including GDPR, HIPAA,
   DORA, NIS2, and US state laws.

 

Governance, Training and Awareness

 * Deliver KLDiscovery’s data protection training and awareness programme.
 * Monitoring changes in privacy laws and advising the organization accordingly.
 * Client and commercial support answering data privacy questions from clients
   as part of client RFPs and due diligence process and questionnaires.
 * Support KLD's AI governance framework and EU AI Act compliance readiness,
   including reviewing AI-driven data processing activities for privacy risk and
   control adequacy.



 

Qualifications and Experience

 * Minimum of 5 years’ experience in a dedicated privacy role, such as a privacy
   manager or equivalent, in an international business, preferably SaaS.
 * A degree in law, information security, IT, compliance, or a related field.
 * Professional certification in data protection or privacy (e.g., CIPP/E, CIPM,
   GDPR Practitioner).
 * Expert knowledge of GDPR, UK Data Protection Act 2018, US State privacy laws
   as well as HIPAA and other relevant legislation.  An AI Act or AI governance
   certification (e.g., AIGP) is an advantage. Experience with ITAR is a plus.
 * Experience conducting security and privacy audits, risk assessments, records
   of processing activities, DPIAs and managing data protection projects.
 * Ability to translate privacy requirements into practical operational guidance
   for product and internal teams.
 * Excellent communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
 * Ability to manage sensitive information with discretion and integrity.

 

Personal Attributes

 * Meticulous attention to detail.
 * Proactive and adaptable approach to work.
 * Ability to work independently and collaboratively.
 * Strong ethical standards and commitment to safeguarding privacy.
 * Confidence to challenge practices and promote compliance across the
   organisation.

 

Reporting Line

The Privacy Manager reports directly to the General Counsel and works closely
with IT, Cybersecurity, Legal, Marketing, Product and People & Culture Teams and
has access to the highest levels of decision-making within the organisation.

 

Location and Working Hours

This position is remote.

 

Remuneration

Competitive salary commensurate with experience, plus benefits package.

 

Our Mission & Values

 

Our Mission: We bring clarity, trust, and meaning to data for clients navigating
legal matters worldwide.

 

These four values guide how we operate, make decisions, and work together every
day.

 * Client is Always in the Room - We operate and make decisions as if the client

### The Role

This is not a traditional design role. We’re looking for a Special Projects Designer.

Ideas, thought leadership and events that take our brand somewhere new, and give us a chance to make things we wouldn’t normally get to make. Things like OFF, our growing mix of editorial content and live events. Seasoned, our platform supporting design education, and CcType, our very own type foundry. These are just the beginning, which is exactly where you come in.

You’ll help us define the ideas, the design and art direction that bring these happenings, digitally and physically to life. As we evolve, these things are becoming bigger and more varied. Events, ventures and content with unexpected collaborations.

This is a unique role for someone entrepreneurial, someone who can spot a good idea, push it further, then further again, then turn it into something people notice, share and talk about. Motion skills are nice to have, but not essential.

You will work closely with Jowey Roden, Koto’s Chief Creative Officer; Dan Witchell, Executive Creative Director in London; and our Global Marketing team, while collaborating with creatives across our global studios. Motion skills are welcome but not essential. What matters most is strong ideas, excellent taste, curiosity and the ability to learn quickly.

Here’s a preview of your playground.

1. You partner closely with Koto’s Chief Creative Officer, London’s Executive Creative Director and Global Marketing team to shape how Koto shows up in the world.
2. You bring a clear creative vision to Koto’s brand, developing strong concepts, visual systems and work that strengthens our reputation and supports our ambitions.
3. You co-lead design across special projects such as Seasoned, CcType and the OFF ecosystem, while helping us imagine and launch new ventures, events, collaborations and products.
4. In a team setting, you take projects from first thought to final delivery, moving confidently between concept development, design, art direction and production.
5. You lead the visual output of Koto’s social channels, creating branded content that earns attention, engages the right audiences and works naturally across platforms.
6. You design across a broad range of formats, including brand identity, campaigns, editorial, events, presentations, digital experiences, merchandise and moving image.
7. You bring fresh thinking to studio launches, cultural moments, hiring campaigns and celebrations, turning them into creative opportunities rather than traditional announcements.
8. You experiment with new tools, formats and production techniques. Motion experience is a plus, but curiosity, initiative and the ability to learn quickly matter more.
9. You work closely with designers, strategists, writers, filmmakers, developers, photographers and external makers, bringing in the right skills to make each idea stronger.

8. We offer access to YCN and fund relevant training opportunities for employees looking to develop their skills and careers.

We build in small, focused initiative teams: a Product Engineer working alongside a PM and a designer, supported by an Engineering Manager who helps you grow. You'll also work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering peers across initiatives in a shared codebase. The whole team owns whether the work moves its metric.

AI coding agents are a force multiplier here — they give a small, senior team the leverage to ship more, faster, and at a higher bar for quality. We hire engineers who are wired for ownership and energized by shipping to a real marketplace with customers and pros on both sides.

**The Role**

You're the engineering anchor of an initiative — working as part of a tight team with your PM and designer, and alongside engineering peers on adjacent initiatives. You have a hand in the full lifecycle: shaping the problem, deciding the technical approach, directing AI agents to implement much of the code, shipping to production, and — with your team — owning the outcome.

You're measured by impact, not by lines of code merged. When an agent can ship something safely, your job is to make sure it's done right and the metric moves. When the work touches a sensitive area, you have the guardrails to prove the change does exactly what it should, with no side effects: strong tests, evals, staged rollouts, and review gates.

**What makes this role exciting:**

* **You ship end-to-end.** From problem-framing through production to the post-launch metric review — you see the whole arc and own the result with your team.
* **You work as a true product partner.** You sit at the table with PM and design, bringing engineering judgment to product calls and product sense to engineering calls.
* **You get real autonomy — with the right checkpoints.** You make most technical calls yourself, with architect review on significant architectural decisions and fast input from peers.

### What You'll Own

* **The technical approach** — architecture, data model, integration choices, rollout plan, observability, and rollback strategy for your initiative. You make most calls yourself and bring significant architectural decisions to architect review; you document them, and revisit if the data says you were wrong.
* **Implementation quality** — the prompts, guardrails, evals, tests, and review loop that let agents ship safe, correct, production-ready code. Most lines will be agent-authored, and you're accountable for them — held to the same standard as the rest of the team working in a shared codebase.
* **Cross-functional partnership** — daily working contact with your PM (scope, tradeoffs) and designer (UX decisions, in-tool prototyping), regular collaboration with engineering peers, and weekly check-ins with your EM.
* **The initiative outcome** — the metric the initiative was set up to move. With your PM, you present results 2–4 weeks post-launch and share the "did it work" answer.
* **A high bar for what ships** — production correctness, security, performance, observability, and the experience for customers and pros. Agents accelerate you; they don't lower the bar.

### Problems to Solve

**Leading AI agents at a staff-level quality bar** Most of the code on your initiative will be authored by AI agents. The craft is making them ship as if a senior engineer wrote it: prompts that encode our conventions, evals that catch issues before merge, tests that exercise the edges, observability that catches a regression before a customer does. How do you build a workflow that lets a small team ship far more than its size would suggest?

**Owning decisions with high autonomy** You have real latitude to make and document technical calls quickly — with architect review on the big architectural ones and peers to pressure-test your thinking. How do you move fast, keep your team aligned, and stay accountable to the outcome?

* **Faster cycle time** — Median time from problem-framing to first production rollout on your initiatives is meaningfully shorter.
* **Quality holds** — No customer- or pro-facing regression traceable to agent-authored code that slipped through your review.

## About Lexerus

Lexerus is an early-stage retail-tech company building AI-powered loss prevention for UK supermarkets and independent retailers.

We're deployed in live stores today, and we're scaling the product, the detection models, and the team.

## The Impact You’ll Make

As our Computer Vision Engineer, you'll own the part of Lexerus that everything else depends on: whether we actually catch theft, and whether we cry wolf while doing it.

You'll work on the full detection stack — person detection and tracking, re-identification across occlusions, behaviour classification, and the suspicion scoring that decides whether a shop manager's phone buzzes. It all runs locally on modest store hardware, so accuracy and inference cost are the same conversation.

This is a hands-on role for someone who wants their models in production under real conditions — bad lighting, awkward camera angles, crowded aisles — rather than on a benchmark leaderboard.

## What You’ll Do

* Own the detection pipeline end-to-end: person detection, multi-object tracking, re-identification, and behaviour classification.
* Fine-tune and evaluate models against real store footage, and build the evaluation sets that tell us whether a change actually helped.
* Drive down false positives — the single metric that decides whether a retailer keeps the system switched on.
* Optimise inference to run reliably on in-store hardware, balancing accuracy against frame rate and cost.
* Build the active-learning loop that turns user feedback on each alert into the next round of training data.
* Work directly with pilot stores to understand why a miss or a false alarm happened, and close the gap.

## Who You Are

* 4+ years building computer vision systems, with models you've taken to production and maintained there.
* Strong Python, and deep practical experience with PyTorch and OpenCV.

LSEG (London Stock Exchange Group) is more than a diversified global financial markets infrastructure and data business. Through a comprehensive suite of trusted financial market infrastructure services – and our open-access model – we provide the flexibility, stability and trust that enable our customers to pursue their ambitions with confidence and clarity.

  

LSEG is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with significant operations in 70 countries across EMEA, North America, Latin America and Asia Pacific. We employ 25,000 people globally, more than half located in Asia Pacific. LSEG’s ticker symbol is LSEG.

  

## **OUR PEOPLE:**

People are at the heart of what we do and drive the success of our business. Our culture of connecting, creating opportunity and delivering excellence shape how we think, how we do things and how we help our people fulfil their potential. We embrace diversity and actively seek to attract individuals with unique backgrounds and perspectives. We break down barriers and encourage teamwork, enabling innovation and rapid development of solutions that make a difference. Our workplace generates an enriching and rewarding experience for our people and customers alike. Our vision is to build an inclusive culture in which everyone feels encouraged to fulfil their potential.

  

We know that real personal growth cannot be achieved by simply climbing a career ladder – which is why we encourage and enable a wealth of avenues and interesting opportunities for everyone to broaden and deepen their skills and expertise. As a global organisation spanning 70 countries and one rooted in a culture of growth, opportunity, diversity and innovation, LSEG is a place where everyone can grow, develop and fulfil your potential with meaningful careers.

  

## **ROLE SUMMARY:**

Help us turn audit findings into lasting improvements! You’ll lead external audit engagement across Group Engineering at LSEG. The role also covers regulatory responses, issues and risk reporting. Bring these services together through safe use of artificial intelligence (AI) across Governance, Risk and Compliance.

  

Reporting to the Head of Technology & Cyber GRC, you’ll set priorities and lead managers, specialists and analysts. This is a first-line role, working with management to address risk. Independent assurance remains with the audit and assurance teams.

  

**WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:**

**Lead external audit engagement.** Manage the relationship with external auditors and bring Finance, control owners and application teams together. Coordinate planning, scope discussions, readiness, evidence requests, walkthroughs and support for testing. Review observations and management responses. Resolve evidence gaps, resolve disagreements and supervise remediation through to closure.

  

**Be responsible for internal audit and regulatory responses.** Prioritise Engineering’s response to internal audits, regulatory examinations and enquiries, and relevant client or contractual assessments. Check evidence and responses, agree owners and track commitments. Keep leaders advised of concerns and decisions needed.

  

**Challenge issues and remediation.** Review self-identified issues and audit or regulatory findings. Question root causes, proposed actions and closure evidence. Confirm that remediation reduces the underlying risk, rather than just completing an action plan. Identify repeat weaknesses and resolve delays. Coordinate risk acceptances through agreed approval routes.

  

**Make risk information useful.** Maintain a consistent Technology and Cyber risk profile and clear risk and control indicators. Use source-system signals to flag emerging risks and breaches of agreed risk limits. Guide risk committees and provide concise Board and executive reporting. Explain what has changed, why it matters and what leaders need to decide.

  

**Improve delivery through AI.** Lead the team that builds and maintains AI agents for GRC evidence gathering, analysis and reporting. Choose use cases and work with engineers or delivery partners. Keep agent logic and change knowledge in-house. Assign owners and set limits on agent access and actions. Test output quality and require human approval for material conclusions. Manage logging, changes, incidents and retirement. You do not need to be the lead engineer.

  

**Develop people and services.** Recruit and mentor colleagues across audit, risk, data and AI governance. Set clear expectations, invite different views and help people build new skills. Measure service quality, reduce rework and focus effort on the highest risks.

  

**WHAT YOU'LL BRING:**

ESSENTIAL SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

External audit experience is essential. We’re looking for the following:

* You have led external audit engagements from planning to closure. Your examples show direct responsibility for evidence quality, findings and management responses.
* You understand Technology and Cyber controls and the evidence auditors and regulators expect. You can assess risk appetite and interpret risk and control indicators.
* You have managed audit, regulatory or remediation portfolios in regulated environments. You challenge weak root causes and check that corrective action reduces risk.
* You have built or improved a risk, audit or GRC capability and developed teams with different specialisms.
* You can weigh evidence, provide direction and explain technical or regulatory issues to senior leaders. You build constructive relationships while challenging conclusions when needed.
* You understand AI risks and controls well enough to oversee agent development and maintenance. You can question engineers on data access, testing, reliability and human oversight.

  

USEFUL EXPERIENCE:

Experience with statutory or financial-statement technology audits is particularly useful. So is work with Information Technology General Controls (ITGCs) or Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (ICOFR). Internal audit experience, financial-services knowledge and early-warning analytics would also help. Relevant accounting, audit, technology-risk or cyber-security qualifications are welcome, alongside equivalent experience.

  

## **WHAT YOU'LL GET IN RETURN:**

Set the direction for your services and build a team with the skills to deliver them. Work directly with senior Engineering, Cyber Security and Finance leaders, auditors and regulators. Your impact will be visible in better evidence, fewer repeat findings and faster risk decisions. You will also develop experience leading responsible use of AI.

At Loop, we're building far more than iconic earwear. We're creating physical products that help people focus, sleep, recover, connect, and thrive.

As our Senior Product Manager, you'll take ownership of a next-generation physical product and help define what's next. You'll turn customer insights, market data, and technical trends into products people love, leading every phase from idea to in-market success while bringing teams together around a clear product vision.

Working across Design, Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, and Commercial, you'll help launch a product that changes how people hear their world.

## **The Role**

You'll shape the future of Loop's product line. You'll own product definition, align technical and business goals, and drive execution across hardware development—from concept and prototyping to tooling, production, and launch.

From early-stage discovery to post-launch iteration, you'll translate insights into decisions, guide trade-offs across engineering, industrial design, manufacturing, and operations, and keep the product on track. You balance imagination with precision—creating space for innovation while keeping delivery sharp.

This is a hands-on role where you'll be on-site 3–4 days a week, closely involved in the physical development of the product—working with prototypes, materials, and samples you can hold in your hands.

## **What You'll Do**

* Define the product vision using customer insights, market data, and technical trends
* Build the business case and roadmap to guide development and align stakeholders
* Lead trade-off decisions across design, engineering, manufacturing, and operations
* Anticipate late-stage challenges (e.g., regulatory compliance, tooling and production readiness, quality iteration) and manage resolution
* Set success metrics and use them to track impact and guide improvements
* Communicate strategy and updates clearly across all levels
* Mentor other PMs and contribute to the evolution of Loop's product management craft

* Build products based on assumptions instead of validated customer needs
* Focus on delivery without shaping product direction
* Wait for perfect certainty before prototyping, testing, and iterating
* Work in silos rather than aligning teams around a shared vision
* Prefer clear answers over navigating ambiguity
* Treat manufacturing and operations as someone else's problem

* Clear communication is one of your strengths. Whether working with leadership or cross-functional teams, you simplify complexity, create alignment, and keep everyone focused on what matters most.

* Prefer following a roadmap over helping define it

## Description

**About Marcura:**

Marcura is a global leader in maritime technology and operations, supporting nearly one-third of the world's seaborne commodity trade. Our trusted platforms which span software, data intelligence and payments sit at the centre of digital transformation across the maritime industry. We are now seeking a Principal Product Manager Compliance to join our high-impact team and contribute to the success of one of the sector's most forward-looking organisations.

**Purpose of Role**

As Principal Product Manager for Marcura Compliance, you own the product strategy, roadmap and commercial outcomes for our compliance portfolio - counterparty due diligence (KYB & KYC), continuous counterparty and vessel monitoring, sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening, cargo screening, and the Counterparty Passport directory. You set direction across the compliance platform, its customer-facing applications and the entity data layer that underpins them, translating regulatory obligatiosn and customer risk appetite into products that maritime, trade and financial institutions rely on to make counterparty decisions.

This is a hands-on principal role rather than a people-management one. You are expected to operate autonomously with minimal direction: you frame the problem, evidence the business case with real usage, billing and market data, define the solution with engineering and compliance specialists, and stay accountable through launch, adoption and revenue. You bring the rigor of financial services compliance (AML/CFT, KYC/KYB, sanctions and financial crime) and apply it to a maritime and trade context, acting as the senior product voice with customers, partners and the executive team.

**Job Responsibilities**

1. Own, publish and defend the multi-year product strategy and roadmap for the Marcura Compliance portfolio, so that investment is directed at the highest-return opportunities, by grounding every decision in measured customer usage, billing and competitive evidence rather than opinion.

2. Define and continuously prioritize the product backlog across the compliance platform and its customer-facing applications, to keep engineering focused on the work that moves revenue and retention, by maintaining a single ranked roadmap and declining work that does not clear the bar.

3. Grow the established revenue lines (KYB onboarding, continuous screening/monitoring, due diligence reporting) to meet agreed ARR targets, by identifying and closing scope, coverage and volume expansion within named accounts together with Sales and Customer Success.

4. Lead the introduction of new propositions, notably the Counterparty Passport directory and embedded compliance across Marcura's other business units, so the portfolio grows beyond its current base, by carrying each one from business case through pilot to first paying customers against agreed dates.

5. Own pricing and packaging for the portfolio, to protect margin and simplify the commercial conversation, by maintaining an evidenced rate card and testing every proposed change against realized prices before it is put to the business.

**Qualifications and Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Law, Computer Science or a related discipline.

**Work Experience**

* 10+ years of total professional experience, including at least 6 years in product management and 3+ years at lead or principal level owning a revenue-bearing product line end to end.
* Substantial experience gained in banking, payments or financial services - ideally in financial crime compliance (AML/CFT, KYC/KYB, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring) or in a RegTech serving those institutions.
* Proven track record of taking a compliance, risk or data product from strategy through discovery and delivery to commercialization, with measurable revenue, adoption or retention outcomes.

Designing for money means designing for trust. Our customers are shop owners, traders and entrepreneurs, and many are new to digital products. They work on low-end devices and unreliable networks, where one confusing screen can cost them a sale. Your team's work has to hold up for them, whatever their ability or device. You make sure it does.

As a Design Manager, you'll lead a small team of product designers and be accountable for everything they ship: its quality, how it works as one product, and the results it drives for our customers and the business.  
Your team works either on the products our customers use on POS, mobile and web, or on the operational tools our teams use to serve them.

It is a hands-on role: you build the systems the team works within and step into the hardest problems yourself.

**What you’ll do**

* Set the design direction for your area, turn it into plans with milestones and measurable outcomes, and make the case for it to senior leaders in customer and business terms.
* Work with product partners so every designer begins from a clear, well-framed brief, and push back early when one isn't ready.
* Keep each customer journey whole across teams, and resolve conflicting designs before they launch.
* Run critique and design reviews against a definition of done that includes accessibility, and stay close enough to the work that nothing reaches customers below the bar.
* Decide what must be tested with customers before build and what can ship and be measured after, and plan that validation into delivery with success metrics defined up front.
* Make sure journeys use the design system, with market and product variations handled inside it rather than as one-off rebuilds.
* Plan and staff system contributions like any other project.
* Build trusted partnerships with product and engineering, so design shapes what gets built, and design and engineering stay in step through build.
* Hire well, set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and build a growth path for each designer.
* Bring AI tools into the team's design process, model effective and responsible use in your own work, and build that fluency across the team.

**What you need to succeed**

* 10+ years of experience in product design, with a portfolio of shipped work across mobile and web that shows the problem, your decisions and the results.
* 3+ years of experience managing product designers, including hiring, coaching and career development.
* Experience setting design direction for a product area and leading a team to deliver it.
* Experience running a design quality practice, such as critique, design reviews and a definition of done, that raised the quality of shipped work. Experience building shared patterns or templates adopted across teams, products or markets.
* Experience shipping accessible, inclusive products for people with disabilities, people new to digital products and people on limited devices and connectivity.
* Experience using AI tools in design work and building that fluency across a team.
* Experience designing for POS terminals is a strong plus.
* Experience in financial services, multiple markets or operational tools is also welcome.

**What you’ll get**

* A leadership role in shaping the future of fintech - your work will influence design strategy and impact millions of users.
* Opportunities for career growth - mentorship, leadership development, and the ability to scale and shape a high-performing design team.
* Autonomy and influence - own design decisions, drive cross-functional collaboration, and define best practices.
* A high-performing and collaborative team - work alongside talented designers, engineers, and product managers in a culture that values design excellence.
* A culture of experimentation - we encourage bold ideas, rapid iteration, and data-driven design improvements.
* Competitive compensation and benefits.
* Remote-friendly work culture with support for professional development and engagement with the design community.

**What to expect in the hiring process**

* Application & portfolio review: we assess your experience, leadership impact, and UX case studies that demonstrate strategic thinking, process, and measurable outcomes.
* Preliminary phone call with recruiter: a brief conversation to discuss your background, leadership experience, and expectations.
* Interview with senior leadership: a deep dive into your leadership approach, design philosophy, and ability to drive impact. This includes a discussion on past projects and collaboration with cross-functional teams.
* Design leadership challenge: a scenario-based assessment to assess both strategic thinking and leadership skills while balancing UX/UI expertise.
* Final executive conversation: a discussion with senior leadership to assess alignment with our vision, strategic thinking, and team-building philosophy.

**How to apply:**

Submit your resume and portfolio showcasing your leadership in managing design teams, driving strategy, and delivering user-centred solutions with measurable business impact. We want to see case studies that demonstrate how you have led and developed designers, prioritised and managed projects, and fostered a high-performing team culture. Your portfolio should highlight how you have used research, data, and experimentation to inform decisions, optimise workflows, and drive success metrics.

💰  Salary range of £31,100 - £39,350 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance

🎂 We guarantee to approve time off on your birthday if it falls on a scheduled work day (outside of your training period).

📍 This role is fully remote and based within the UK.

📚 A £1,000 annual budget to spend on books, training courses, and conferences.

**Job Description for Technology and Cyber Services - Security Operations Manager:**

There’s never been a more exciting time to be part of the nuclear sector. New opportunities are being created all the time. At UKNNL, you’ll be in the ideal place to capitalise on this momentum, face new challenges and develop a long, successful and meaningful career.

We’re an organisation that’s here to experiment and push the limits of what’s possible. So, if you’re keen to excel in your chosen field, this is the place to do it. Because at UKNNL, anything is possible.

The Security Operations Manager, working within UKNNL’s Technology and Cyber Services (TCS) team, is accountable for leading, developing, and continuously improving UKNNL’s end-to-end security operations capability, ensuring the organisation can effectively prevent, detect, respond to, and recover from cyber and information security threats.

The location for this role is flexible and can be based at Risley, Workington or Preston.

**Main Responsibilities **for Technology and Cyber Services - Security Operations Manager:****

* Manage a small SecOps team, providing support, direction, leadership, coaching and mentoring to maximise performance and ensure team wellbeing.
* Help ensure SecOps activities are prioritised and aligned to organisational risk appetite and CISO strategy.
* Act as a leader within the Sec Ops area – possibly deputising if required for the wider section Head; also providing SME advice as required to the TCS senior team. This will include representing SecOps at related UKNNL governance and security meetings.
* Maintain and develop governance, reporting, and performance management frameworks to drive accountability and continuous improvement.
* Own and continuously improve UKNNL’s end-to-end security monitoring, detection, and response capability, ensuring effective coordination between internal teams and external providers. This includes strong emphasis on understanding Security Operations best practice and emerging best practice, and being able to help drive performance and value from security partners and suppliers (intelligent customer) - the role will require the ability to represent UKNNL at performance review meetings with key SecOps partners.
* If required, lead the operational management of security incidents, including larger incidents, helping ensure timely containment, recovery, and communication. Support post-incident learning to strengthen resilience and reduce future risk.
* Define and help deliver a structured security testing and exercising programme to validate the effectiveness of security controls across people, process, and technology.
* Lead the ongoing maturity and evolution of security operations capabilities, including processes, tooling, and resources; this will include understanding baseline activity to help further develop detection rules and process.
* Develop and implement roadmaps aligned to strategic objectives and emerging threats – being actively aware of threat landscape, vulnerabilities, risks, and mitigations.
* As required, operate flexibly, to provide input and support to other cyber and information security sections of TCS, helping manage risk, remain compliant and support business delivery.

**Essential Criteria **for Technology and Cyber Services - Security Operations Manager:****

* Experience in cyber security operations within regulated or critical infrastructure environments.
* Proven leadership of security operations teams and/or managed security services (SOC/MSOC).
* Experience managing security incidents and crisis-level response; able to operate under pressure.
* Strong understanding of incident response and digital forensics.
* Strong understanding of threat intelligence and threat hunting.
* Strong understanding of vulnerability management and security controls.
* Strong understanding security testing, assurance, and audit practices.
* Experience working with regulators, auditors, and compliance frameworks.
* Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into operational capability.
* Experience managing third-party suppliers and service providers.
* Degree or higher in a related subject.
* Evidence of related relevant operations certifications and training.
* Ability to obtain SC level security clearance (this includes but is not limited to identity, employment, financial and criminal record checks plus 5 years’ worth of UK residency).

**Desirable Criteria **for Technology and Cyber Services - Security Operations Manager:****

* Membership of a cyber security or related professional body.

UKNNL isn’t just a place where you can do career-defining work that makes a real-world impact. It’s also a place where you’ll feel appreciated and valued. UKNNL is an incredible place to work. A place where people do things that have never been done before. A place where people push boundaries to further themselves, the business and society as a whole.

**Job Description for Security and Resilience Officer:**

There’s never been a more exciting time to be part of the nuclear sector. New opportunities are being created all the time. At UKNNL, you’ll be in the ideal place to capitalise on this momentum, face new challenges and develop a long, successful and meaningful career.

We’re an organisation that’s here to experiment and push the limits of what’s possible. So, if you’re keen to excel in your chosen field, this is the place to do it. Because at UKNNL, anything is possible.

The Security & Resilience Support Officer supports the delivery of security, regulatory compliance and resilience arrangements across the Uranium Research Centre (Preston) and the Nuclear Materials Research Centre and Active Handling Centre (Sellafield). The role is primarily based at Sellafield and is responsible for the management of security systems, maintenance of local security arrangements, security risk assessment activities, implementation of security assurance arrangements and support to emergency exercises to ensure security requirements are effectively maintained. Limited travel to other laboratory facilities may be required

**Main Responsibilities for Security and Resilience Officer:**

* Maintain detailed knowledge of local security arrangements and support the development, implementation and review of security contingency plans.
* Administer and maintain physical security systems, including Intruder Detection Systems (IDS), Automatic Access Control Systems (AACS) and CCTV systems, ensuring faults, maintenance activities, user permissions and testing requirements are appropriately managed.
* Support the development, review and maintenance of Security Risk Assessments and associated security documentation.
* Coordinate and administer temporary security arrangements in accordance with Nuclear Site Security Plan (NSSP) requirements and local procedures.
* Conduct security inspections, audits and assurance activities, recording findings and supporting the implementation and tracking of corrective actions.
* Maintain security records, registers, appointments and governance documentation to support security management and assurance activities.
* Provide security advice and guidance to facility personnel, project teams and other stakeholders and act as a local point of contact for routine security matters.
* Support the planning, delivery and review of emergency exercises, ensuring security arrangements are appropriately represented and tested.
* Support the investigation of security incidents, events and concerns, including the identification and implementation of corrective actions.
* Contribute to the continuous improvement of security arrangements through the identification of lessons learned, emerging risks and improvement opportunities.

**Essential Criteria for Security and Resilience Officer:**

* Detail orientated, and able to work to stringent deadlines within a project delivery environment, whilst always maintaining discretion.
* Detailed knowledge and understanding of the Nuclear Industries Security Regulations (NISR 2003) and its applicability.
* Experience of security decision-making and security systems management.
* Experience of implementing security modifications on the Sellafield site, including stakeholder management.
* High levels of integrity and confidence to challenge the behaviour of others.
* Evidence of self-motivation with demonstrable levels of drive, energy, and resilience.
* Ability to communicate key information both verbal and written with customers, suppliers, and stakeholders.
* Ability to be appointed as Security & Regulatory Liaison Officer (SLO & RLO).
* Ability to obtain DV level security clearance (this includes but is not limited to identity, employment, financial, criminal record checks, interview plus 10 years of UK residency).

**Desirable Criteria for Security and Resilience Officer:**

* Experienced working in a regulated environment.
* Experience of supporting emergency exercises or emergency preparedness activities in a major accident industry.
* Level 4 qualification (or equivalent experience) in an emergency planning or security discipline.
* A thorough awareness of nuclear, conventional safety and security requirements applicable to their area(s) of responsibility.
* Experience in Change Management including influencing and persuading large teams.
* Experience of working with sensitive information assets and the management of Classified Documents Registers.

Shaping the world by connecting markets to optimise the worlds valuable resources. With a global team of more than 700, ICIS has employees based in London, New York, Houston, Karlsruhe, Frankfurt, Milan, Mumbai, Singapore, Guangzhou, Beijing, Shanghai, Dubai, Sao Paulo, Seoul, and Tokyo.

Are you passionate about applying data science, AI and analytics to solve complex business problems and create products that customers love?
At ICIS, we're building the next generation of data-driven and AI-powered solutions for global commodity markets. As a Lead Data Scientist, you will join 30+ experienced Data Scientists in our Analytics Hubs in Karlsruhe or London. Our Data Science group create forecast models, predictive data and interactive analytical tooling for trading and scenario planning. We model commodity markets with a wide range of techniques from fundamental market modelling, statistical to machine learning & AI, mathematical optimisation / linear programming, system dynamics and agent-based models. We work in small teams with a high degree of ownership and direct collaboration with customers.
In your role, you will primarily focus on creating market-leading predictive models and interactive analytics for market fundamentals, prices, supply, demand & trade in the context of Chemicals, the global supply network for petrochemical commodities, recycling materials and their end-use applications. You will coordinate, guide and project-manage other Data Scientists, and take full ownership for delivering high-quality Data Science solutions.

Create and continuously improve analytical commodity market models in Python: Co-develop with our analysts & engineers strong quantitative market models, such as demand modelling, supply modelling for capacity & cost, storage, trade & transport modelling, market balance & market price forecasting
Guide, project-manage, develop & retain our market modelling talent. Align work and business outcomes with stakeholders. Perspective to take on people management responsibility once proven
Connect, clean, and impute freight, pricing, and supply/demand datasets from diverse internal and external sources. Turn raw, imperfect and incomplete data into actionable market insight

Work goal-driven and self-organized with own project management responsibility on developments from day 1
Guide and support others in the development of models as well as create hands-on own implementations of framework enhancements. Actively share components, knowledge & innovation with peers
Key Skills/Experience Required:
Minimum of 5 years of practical experience in predictive modelling in the context of (commodity) markets or trading, supply, demand and prices. Knowledge of assumption-based scenario modelling as well as marginal supply cost curves
Experience to work as a team goal driven directly with internal/external customers to identify & solve high-value business problems, self-organised. Strong communication and engagement, ability to explain complex concepts simply to stakeholders
Production-ready code in Python and SQL, using AI-code generation and Spec-Driven-Development in a productive & manageable way, familiar with common Data Science & analytics libraries
Data modelling, transformation, and visualization (eg Python Dash)
Experience with software development (modularisation, versioning eg with GIT, tests, understandable code), with containerization (Docker) and orchestration (Airflow)
Habit of starting simple first to get buy-in early and iterate on feedback to add value
Curiosity & desire to understand the world
A plus: existing knowledge of the chemical industry, Databricks & Snowflake

Work on Problems That Matter: global organizations make better decisions using data, analytics and AI 
Build the Future of AI in commodity markets: Play a key role in shaping next-generation AI products and capabilities that will influence the future of our business and our industry 
Work with Exceptional People: Join a multidisciplinary team of data scientists, engineers, economists, industry experts and product leaders who are passionate about innovation and customer impact

# Chief of Staff

## Location

Nous HQ

## Employment Type

Full time

## Location Type

Hybrid

## Department

Central (General & Administrative)

OverviewApplication

## **About Nous**

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

## **Why we're hiring**

Nous runs on small teams with real ownership and barely any middle management. That's a big part of how about 30 of us became one of the UK's fastest-growing startups. It also means the work of joining everything up has been spread across the founders and leads, squeezed in around their day jobs. Plans, OKRs, closing the hires that matter, the big company pushes: everyone does a bit of it and nobody owns it.

Last week showed what happens when someone does. We ran "crunch week": five days where most of the company dropped its normal work to relaunch Nous as a household agent. Twelve workstreams, one owner each, a short daily sync and a pre-mortem. In a week we rebuilt onboarding and the website, shipped new agent capabilities, and got legal, security and comms ready for launch. As one of the team said afterwards, when we cluster around a problem for a bit, we do loads of work.

We want that pace more of the time, without a founder having to drop everything to run it. So we're hiring a Chief of Staff.

## **About the role**

You'll work directly with Greg (our CEO) and the founding team, and own how Nous runs day to day: the pace, planning and OKRs, and the big company pushes, plus overseeing hiring and helping land the hires that matter most. You'll sit in the management meeting and get the full picture, including the things that aren't public yet. And you'll have the authority to change how we work: cancel or reshape meetings, and move people and cut scope during a big push.

You enjoy coordinating, but only because it gets things done faster. You'd rather get a decision made today than design a process for making decisions.

## **What you'll actually do**

* Set the pace. Spot what's stuck, work out why, and get it moving. Usually it's a decision nobody has made yet, so you get it made, or make it yourself.
* Own planning and OKRs. Quarterly OKRs, the weekly management meeting, planning and offsites. Squads run pretty autonomously; you make sure they're working to the same priorities. Each of these should take up less of everyone's time with you running it, not more.
* Own the scorecard. Keep the numbers behind our OKRs current, and say each week what's off track and why. You pull the data yourself (SQL, our BI tool, a spreadsheet) rather than chasing people for updates.
* Run the big pushes. The next crunch week is yours: scope it with the leadership team, pick the owners, run it, and write up what we'd do differently next time.
* Oversee hiring, and help close the hires that matter. Hiring managers run their own processes, and you won't be running ten of them. But you'll keep an eye on all of them, know where every search stands, and jump in where needed. Mostly that's closing the people we really want: working out what they care about and how to win them. Sometimes it's getting a recruiter excited about working with Nous, or unsticking a process that's gone quiet.
* Represent Nous. You'll talk to recruiters and senior candidates from day one. Over time, and where it helps, you'll represent us to partners, suppliers and investors too.
* Automate the boring bits. You'd rather build the Monday status digest with Claude than write it by hand every week. Anything you find yourself doing every week is a candidate for automating.

## **What this role isn't**

* An assistant. Diaries and inboxes are someone else's job.
* A process role. If your first instinct is a new meeting, template or tracker, this probably won't suit you. With you here we should have fewer recurring meetings, not more.
* A product role. Squads own what gets built, and strategy stays with the founders. You'll be in the room for both, and you make sure nobody's blocked.
* A recruiter. You oversee hiring and step in where it matters; hiring managers still run their own processes.
* A dumping ground for jobs nobody else wants. You'll pick up odd jobs, as everyone here does, but the bulk of the role is above.

## **What success looks like**

In your first 90 days:

* The company runs noticeably better: decisions get made faster and fewer things stall. Ask the leads and they'd say so.
* Something that had been stuck for weeks has shipped because you got involved.
* You've helped close at least one hire we really wanted.
* Next quarter's OKRs are set, and the scorecard is current every week.
* At least one piece of weekly coordination (the OKR update, the status round-up) runs as an AI workflow you built, and nobody does it by hand any more.
* We have fewer recurring meetings than when you joined.

After a year:

* You've led two or three company-wide pushes that shipped what they set out to.
* The senior hires you helped close have said yes and are doing well.
* Planning, OKRs and the weekly meetings run fine for a month without you.
* Most of the routine coordination runs on workflows and tools you built, not on meetings.

## **About you**

You've got 4–7 years behind you (perhaps a little more if you've switched careers), probably a mix of a fast-growing startup and somewhere that taught you structure: consulting, BizOps or strategy and ops at a scale-up, a founder's office, or product work where you ran launches across teams. Maybe you've founded something.

You coordinate because you're impatient. You notice the thing that's been stuck for a week, and you're the one who unsticks it.

You're persuasive. You can work out what a candidate is really optimising for and how to close them, get a busy recruiter excited about Nous, and hold your own with senior people outside the company.

You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a quick model, write a bit of SQL or find the right dashboard, and tell a real trend from noise.

AI tooling is already how you work. Claude, Claude Code or similar is where you get things done, not something you tried once.

You write clearly and quickly. Most of this job happens in writing: kick-off notes, weekly updates, closing emails.

You tell people the truth, founders included, and you keep confidences. You'll see salaries, plans and people issues before anyone else does.

You listen and you care, but you don't do politics. This role has more connective tissue with others than anyone else in the business, so by playing it straight and being an honest broker, you are also establishing an important norm.

Low ego. Some of the job is unglamorous and you do it anyway.

Bonus points:

* You've closed hard candidates, or worked in recruiting, talent or BD.
* You've run a company planning cycle, an offsite or a launch end to end.
* You've worked somewhere regulated (energy, fintech, insurance).
* You've automated a chunk of your own job and have something to show for it.
* You are commercially astute or professionally experienced in a deep domain like law or accounting.

## **How you will grow**

This might not be a forever role, and that's fine.
