## **About Nous**

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

## **How we build (worth reading before the role)**

How products get built is changing fast. With AI tooling, a PM can prototype, dig into production data and commit production code to get a change live all in an afternoon. An engineer can own a product area end to end and decide what to build next.

We're leaning into that. Our PMs lean into code and our engineers run products: one of our engineers owns the car insurance targets. We care about whatever gets the job done most effectively, regardless of once upon a time whose job it was meant to be.

We're moving fast and adapting as we go, and we don't have all the answers yet. What should a squad look like when everyone can build? Where does process still help, and where does it just slow you down? What's a PM for when an engineer can run the experiment themselves? We're working it out, and we want someone who is excited to be part of helping figure it out.

## **About the role**

So where does a PM fit? A lot of our work still suits squads: clear targets, a few service lines and a team of engineers. Those squads need product managers to run them. All our roles in product overlap, but this one is centred on product management. If you’d rather spend all your time building, have a look at our Product Builder role.

You’ll take a squad responsible for a key section of our product and service lines and grow them: expand what they cover, understand the levers that drive their performance (automation, new suppliers, what we recommend to members) and increase their commercial value.

Being a Product Manager at Nous is one of the hardest roles we have. The product is complex and we move fast, so you need to be able to hold a lot of context. You'll switch between very different things all day: thinking about OKRs and the plan for the next couple of weeks one moment, getting a PR into production the next, while helping unblock an engineer.

That's also what makes it exciting.

You bring order to fast-moving work, get some sequencing in place so people aren’t each figuring it out on their own, evaluate what’s being shipped, own the reporting and keep the squad’s energy up. You won’t hesitate to make changes yourself, but you won’t be just another builder in the squad either: when you’re heads-down building, you can’t unblock anyone or bring the team together.

Growing a service line here means working across the boundary between product and commercial, so we’re particularly interested in PMs who’ve had real exposure to the commercial side of a business.

Our agent acts in the real world a lot, so saving someone money takes more than great product execution. We also need access to the best tariffs and suppliers, and we have to understand the regulation we operate in. And because Nous is an agent, your nice neat Amplitude funnels don't work: every user's journey can be totally different. So we're after PMs who are excited by everything it takes to make an agentic product work for real households, including the bits that wouldn't traditionally count as "product".

Worth being upfront: we can't tell you yet which service lines you'd own. It depends on the Venn diagram of your particular skill set and the problems we need to solve at the point you join.

## **What matters most**

We need all of these at once:

* Sharp. You pick things up quickly and enjoy hard problems. Given a messy one, you can lay out what you know and what you'd check first, then change your mind as new data turns up.
* Adaptable. We’re working a lot of this out as we go, so the role and the squad will change, probably more than once. You enjoy that. You pick up whatever’s needed, PM work or not, and you work in the open: sharing rough thinking early and changing course when someone has a better idea.
* Delivery. You bring order to a fast-moving squad: clear priorities, sensible sequencing, people unblocked quickly, and an honest look at whether what shipped actually worked.
* Product craft. You find the real problem behind a request and make the trade-offs explicit. You care about the details of what our users actually see.
* Commercial and analytical. You know what your area made last month, what moved it and what you'd do next, and you answer most of your own questions with data. You think in conversion, margin and lifetime value as readily as in features.
* Energy. You've probably worked at a startup. You move fast, you're happy doing the unglamorous work yourself, and you'd rather ship this week's version than polish next quarter's.

And everyone builds here, PMs included. You'll use AI tooling (Claude Code or whatever gets it done) to prototype, dig into data and ship changes yourself. You don't need to be an engineer, but you shouldn't be scared of code.

## **What you'll actually do**

* Grow your service lines. Understand what really drives their performance, be able to measure it, and lead the squad to deliver it.
* Set the squad's OKRs and roadmap, get the sequencing in place, and drive fast, efficient execution.
* Evaluate what’s being shipped, and own the reporting: make sure the reports and the data behind them make sense.
* Work across product and commercial: the suppliers and tariffs we can offer, the regulation we work within, and what that means for what gets built.
* Run experiments, and unblock yourself on the analysis without always needing an analyst.
* Get close to members and ops. Read the conversations, sit with the people handling the edge cases, and fix the parts of the journey where people drop out or get stuck.

## **About you**

You'll likely thrive here if:

* You've been a PM for a few years, ideally at a startup, and you've owned something with a number attached: revenue, conversion, retention.
* You've worked on the commercial side as well as the product side: a P&L, a supplier or partner relationship, pricing, or a whole service line.

This probably isn't for you if your PM experience is mostly roadmaps and stakeholder management at a big company, with no number you owned.

## **How we work**

We keep the middle thin, on purpose. There's barely any middle management, which means fewer bottlenecks and room for exceptional people to have real impact without first being promoted into managing others. It's a real bet, not a free lunch. Instead of a manager buffer, you get lots of context and colleagues who help because they're invested, not because an org chart says so. If you need a clear remit handed down before you can move, this probably won't suit you.

Your first 90 days are built around getting you to real ownership safely: pairing when you want it, lots of context, and people who want you to ship. We celebrate the person who built the unglamorous version this week, not whoever thought of it first.

# Clinical Safety & Workflow Specialist

Shape the boundaries, escalation rules, and evidence that keep operational automation useful without letting it drift into clinical judgement.

London · Hybrid · Full-time

Working pattern**Hybrid, with clinic time**

Type**Full-time**

## Why this role exists

Clinic workflows sit close to clinical decisions even when the work itself is administrative. A patient can reply to a booking message with a symptom, a routine result can need urgent review, and a harmless-looking exception can change the risk entirely.

You will bring clinical reasoning into product and implementation decisions. The role is not to make software practise medicine. It is to make sure the system recognises where operational work ends, stops cleanly, and reaches the right qualified person.

## What you will do

* Review proposed workflows for clinical touchpoints, foreseeable misuse, ambiguous language, and escalation needs.
* Define boundaries for automatic action, human approval, clinician routing, and hard stops with the clinic's own responsible team.
* Build representative safety scenarios and acceptance criteria for replies, results, urgency signals, vulnerable patients, and uncertain matches.
* Review patient-facing drafts and templates for clarity, scope, tone, and unintended clinical meaning.
* Participate in release reviews, incident learning, rule changes, and periodic audits of live workflow behaviour.
* Help clinic teams understand their role in safe operation, including what to monitor, how to pause, and when to escalate.

# **About Oneleet**

Oneleet is one of the fastest-growing security and compliance platforms in history. Having just raised a **$33 million Series A**, we are rapidly growing in customers and employees. Our team has decades of experience in security and compliance. Join our team of opinionated rebels and help us build a category-defining company reshaping the broken and fragmented compliance and cybersecurity industry.

## **Who we’re looking for:**

We value passionate self-starters with a growth mindset and a bias for action and personal accountability. If you love solving hard problems, thrive in ambiguity, and want to make a real impact, you’ll fit right in.

We’re especially drawn to:

* Rebels with a cause — frustrated with the status quo and eager to disrupt it.
* Opinionated (but not obstinate) builders — decisive yet collaborative, who help us move fast.
* Clear communicators — who own their ideas and follow through.

Our mission is simple: make effective cybersecurity painless. We believe cybersecurity should empower, not burden. This belief unites our team and drives every decision we make.

If you’re ready to challenge the status quo and help shape the future of cybersecurity, we’d love to meet you.

# The Role

Oneleet helps customers understand the security posture of the vendors they use without repeating the same research for every company. Our shared vendor library brings together findings from public sources so customers can make informed decisions faster.

As our Vendor Supply Chain Analyst, you’ll help build and maintain that library. Your core responsibility is verifying AI-generated research: checking findings against saved sources, resolving gaps, and making sure the evidence supports the conclusions. Engineering owns the AI research pipeline; you’ll provide the feedback that makes its output more accurate and useful.

Each shared vendor record has a security posture score. Customer-specific risk scores are calculated separately using each customer’s exposure to that vendor. Your work ensures the underlying vendor research is reliable.

Preliminary research results appear immediately. Human verification follows, with a target turnaround of 1-2 days. The pipeline automatically re-researches vendors every 90 days and routes significant changes for human review.

You’ll help work through an initial backlog of approximately 500–600 vendors, prioritizing those used by the most customers. You’ll also help establish how we measure research accuracy and compare computed scores with existing customer-assigned ratings. This is an opportunity to shape how Oneleet evaluates vendor security at scale.

# Key Responsibilities

* **Verify vendor research.** Check AI-generated findings against saved sources, prioritizing vendors by how many customers use them. Correct unsupported claims and distinguish confirmed findings from missing or inconclusive evidence.
* **Build and maintain the vendor library.** Research new SaaS vendors, resolve incomplete records, and review significant changes flagged by the pipeline, including breaches and changes to security practices.
* **Resolve source-access gaps.** When the pipeline cannot fetch a page or encounters a login barrier, find an accessible source or manually upload an available document.
* **Confirm public security claims.** Verify evidence for criteria such as SSO availability, published DPAs, subprocessor lists, and whether a SOC 2 report exists.
* **Measure accuracy and calibrate scoring.** Evaluate research accuracy during the proof of concept and beyond. Compare computed scores with existing customer-assigned ratings, investigate differences, and recommend adjustments where the evidence supports them.
* **Improve research quality.** Document recurring errors, missed evidence, and ambiguous results, then give engineering actionable feedback to improve the AI pipeline.
* **Recommend criteria updates.** Identify gaps or unclear definitions in the evaluation criteria and propose changes as vendor practices and security expectations evolve.
* **Maintain defensible evidence.** Keep findings traceable to saved sources, with clear reasoning and research dates, so customers and auditors can understand the basis for a finding months later.
* **Develop verification runbooks.** Document repeatable review steps and escalation paths that help the team make consistent decisions.

# You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have

* Hands-on experience conducting vendor security due diligence or third-party security assessments.
* Strong research skills and the judgment to distinguish evidence from marketing claims.
* Familiarity with SaaS security practices and public security, privacy, and compliance documentation.
* An analytical mindset and comfort investigating discrepancies, documenting uncertainty, and checking whether a score reflects the underlying evidence.
* Clear written communication and careful documentation habits.
* A self-starter mindset: you take initiative, adapt quickly, thrive in ambiguity, and enjoy building processes from scratch.

# Bonus Points For

* Experience evaluating AI-generated research or designing human review processes.
* Experience measuring research accuracy, calibrating scoring systems, or building quality assurance processes.
* A background in third-party risk, compliance, or security research.
* Experience helping an early-stage startup grow from Seed to Series A or beyond.
* Scripting or automation skills that help you analyze results or make verification more efficient.

# **Why Oneleet?**

At Oneleet, you’ll join a tight-knit team of rebels redefining the cybersecurity industry. We move fast, own our work, and challenge outdated models to make security effortless and effective for companies.

Here’s what makes us special:

* We value impact over titles, autonomy over micromanagement, and clarity over jargon.
* You’ll tackle meaningful, hard problems with real-world consequences.
* You’ll work with smart, kind, and ambitious teammates who lift each other up.

## **Perks & Benefits**

* Comprehensive health & wellness benefits
* 20 days PTO per year, plus 8 floating holiday
* Remote work culture
* Team off-sites in stunning places (Amsterdam, Italy, etc).

We are a senior team, working across the UK and internationally. Teams stay small, everyone works directly with the client, and every build is reviewed by a senior engineer before it reaches them.

Layer deterministic checks over the model's output, business rules and validation a client can inspect, so a guess that breaks the rules is caught by code rather than posted.

Route low-confidence cases to a human with a per-field confidence score, and turn their fixes into new test cases.

Practise eval-driven development, measuring field-level accuracy on a golden set of the client's real documents before anything goes live.

Build it to run inside the client's own cloud, so their documents never leave and nothing you process trains anyone's models, with an audit trail on every run.

Sit with the client to scope the first workflow and agree what good enough to trust actually means.

Comfortable layering deterministic validation over probabilistic output, and building human-in-the-loop review into a workflow.

Familiar with running models in a client's own cloud, model-agnostic, and integrating through existing APIs.

Able to work directly with a client, and to be honest about where AI is and is not reliable.

* The team runs the website, customer campaigns, and events, and Sales owns the deck. You set the positioning and the plan (what's launching, what we call it, why it matters, and who does what), and make the core launch pieces yourself, from the launch copy and one pager to the enablement pack and whatever else the campaign needs.

Plan and run each launch with the rest of marketing: agree the customer adoption plan with our customer marketer, brief content on feature and integrations pages, and line up events, podcasts and social. * Embedded early with product teams: in the roadmap and the specs before anything ships, and trusted by product managers because their launches get better for it.
* The knack of turning a spec, a roadmap entry or a rough demo into positioning people actually use.
* A doer who runs with a goal: sets it up, plans it and delivers it without hand holding or a big team behind them.
* The judgement to stop and ask why: what a launch is meant to achieve, whether it's working, and when to change course.
* A high bar for quality. Fast matters, but what goes out has to be good, and past work shows it.
* Writing that's a real strength: clear, simple and straight to the point. Plain copy over clever copy, fewer words over more.
* Good taste and the skills to make things without waiting on a designer or an agency: a banner, slide, page or short video that looks right. No need to be a designer.
* An AI forward way of working: using AI every day to research, write and make things faster, even building simple tools to make launch assets.

## **About Pleo**

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

**About the role**

We’re looking for a Sales Operations Business Partner to sit between our sales leadership and the systems, data, and processes that run the revenue engine. You’ll help the sales team understand where deals stand, where revenue is coming from, and where it’s at risk. You’ll own how we track pipeline, report on performance, and build the dashboards leaders rely on to make decisions. This is a role for someone who thinks in business outcomes first and uses data and tools as the means to get there.

**What you’ll do**

* Own pipeline management processes, including stage definitions, forecasting cadence, and hygiene standards, and work with sales managers to keep the pipeline accurate.
* Build and maintain regular sales reporting covering bookings, pipeline coverage, conversion rates, win/loss, and rep and team performance.
* Design, build, and maintain dashboards that give leadership and frontline managers a clear view of performance against targets.
* Act as a business partner to sales leaders: understand their priorities, translate them into operational requirements, and bring data-backed recommendations to planning and business reviews.
* Support forecasting and quarterly business reviews by preparing the data, challenging assumptions, and flagging risks early.
* Own day-to-day administration and configuration of the CRM (e.g. Salesforce or HubSpot), including fields, workflows, user access, and reporting structure, in partnership with the RevOps or systems team.
* Drive adoption of CRM and sales processes by working with managers and reps, and by making the right behaviour the easy one.
* Support territory, quota, and compensation-related analysis as needed, in partnership with Finance.
* Identify process gaps and inefficiencies across the sales funnel and lead improvements, documenting changes and training the team on them.
* Work cross-functionally with Marketing, Finance, Customer Success, and Product Ops to keep data consistent across systems.

**What you’ll bring**

* 7+ years of experience in sales operations, revenue operations, GTM operations, or a related commercial role, ideally in a [B2B SaaS / relevant industry] environment.
* Strong experience with CRM systems, ideally Salesforce or HubSpot, including reporting and basic administration.
* Solid understanding of sales metrics and funnel dynamics, including pipeline coverage, conversion, forecasting accuracy, and sales cycle length.
* Proven ability to build clear reports and dashboards in tools such as Excel/Google Sheets, Looker, Tableau, or Power BI. You don’t need to write code, but you should be comfortable working with data and spotting what matters.
* Experience running pipeline reviews or forecast calls, or supporting leaders who do.
* A consultative approach: you can listen to a sales leader, ask the right questions, and turn their needs into a practical solution.
* Strong communication skills, with the ability to present findings clearly to senior stakeholders and explain trade-offs simply.
* Good judgement and attention to detail, with the ability to balance speed and accuracy.
* Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment with multiple priorities.

**Nice to have**

* Experience supporting a sales team through a scaling or transformation phase.
* Familiarity with sales compensation or territory planning tools.
* Exposure to revenue analytics or forecasting methodologies.
* Experience with a BI tool or basic SQL, though this is not required.

**What success looks like**

* Leadership trusts the pipeline and forecast numbers and uses them to make decisions.
* Sales managers run their reviews from the dashboards you’ve built, without needing manual reports.
* CRM data quality improves measurably over time.
* Sales leaders see you as a partner who brings ideas, not just reports.

* **English first.** Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.
* **A fair look for everyone.** Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.
* **Diversity drives us.** We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.
* **Interview at your best.** We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email belonging@pleo.io. We’ll design a process that works for you.

* A qualification in Pharmacy/ work experience as a Pharmacist would be highly beneficial.
* At least 2 years of relevant experience.

* Previous experience working as a Regulatory and Start Up Specialist  or Site Contracts Specialists in either a CRO or pharmaceutical/ biotech industry or equivalent, relevant experience and/or demonstrated competencies.
* Strong communication and organizational skills.
* Experience using computerized information systems, electronic spreadsheets, word processing and electronic mail required.
* Fluency in English

**Preferred:**

* Relevant regulatory and site start-up (feasibility, contract negotiations, CA/ EC/ IRB submissions) experience.
* Experience in site contract and budget negotiation would be a strong plus.
* Experience using milestone tracking tools/systems.
* Ability to prioritize workload to meet deadlines
* Advanced degree in medical or life sciences (MD, PhD, PharmD)/RAC certification/Masters in Regulatory Science.

# Data Analyst — Energy Retail (Oil & Gas)

IT - London, Greater London

About the role

A hands-on analyst for a consumer energy business: pay-as-you-go cooking gas (LPG) delivered to hundreds of thousands of households in fast-growing emerging markets. You own the analysis end to end — framing the question, getting the data, building the numbers and defending them in front of the people who will act on them. You work directly with commercial, operations, finance and management, and with our founders — no account manager in between.

You join our energy data team, alongside a senior data scientist and a data & BI engineer. A meaningful part of the work starts in raw tables, meter logs, payment exports and field-operations files rather than in a tidy warehouse.

We do not require you to come from oil & gas. The business model is much closer to a prepaid mobile operator than to a fuel station: customers top up credit with mobile money, consume in small amounts, and every unit used is recorded by a smart meter. Experience at mobile network operators, telecoms, mobile money or fintech, utilities with prepaid metering, pay-as-you-go solar, and similar high-volume B2C businesses is directly relevant.

What the work looks like

Each customer home has a stove, a smart meter and a gas cylinder owned and maintained by the company. Customers pay only for the gas they use, topping up as little as a single meal’s worth through mobile money, and local technicians replace cylinders before they run out. That produces rich data — consumption, top-ups, cylinder swaps, deliveries, meter events — and commercial questions to match: which customers stay and why, what a customer is worth, where the network makes or loses money, and what to do about it.

Scope

* Customer analytics — acquisition, activation, retention and churn, cohort behaviour, revenue and margin per household, lifetime value against the cost of installation
* Consumption and top-up behaviour — frequency and size of top-ups, usage patterns, seasonality, early signs that a customer is about to go dormant
* Pricing and promotion analysis — the effect of price, top-up incentives and campaigns on usage and margin, measured against proper baselines and control groups
* Field operations and unit economics — cylinder swap and delivery efficiency, depot and area performance, technician productivity, cost to serve per household
* Forecasting gas demand, cylinder logistics and revenue by area, to support supply, stock and expansion decisions
* Anomaly and fraud detection — meter tampering, consumption that does not match cylinder swaps, payment irregularities, unusual field activity
* Reporting with single agreed definitions where commercial, operations and finance count customers, revenue or volume differently
* Messy data as the normal case: meter connectivity gaps, delayed payment records, re-assigned devices, data from more than one country and system

Requirements

* 4+ years as a data analyst or in a comparable analytical role, owning your own analyses from question to recommendation
* Experience with high-volume B2C transactional data — prepaid mobile or telecoms, mobile money, utilities, pay-as-you-go energy, retail or similar. You know what subscriber-, account- or transaction-level data looks like and where it lies
* Commercial analytics in practice: churn and retention, cohort and lifetime-value analysis, segmentation, pricing or campaign evaluation
* Strong SQL and Python (pandas or similar), and readiness to work in raw data yourself: unfamiliar schemas, undocumented tables, exports never meant for analysis
* Sound statistics for business questions — baselines, control groups, seasonality, telling a real effect from noise
* Working with coding agents, seriously. Agents write most of the code here. Bad agent output in analysis fails silently: a join fans out rows, a filter drops half the active customers, a top-up is attributed to the wrong month. We hire for verification habits, not speed — row-count and population checks, reconciliation against a number someone already trusts, a traceable path from raw data to any figure a decision-maker sees
* Experience with a BI tool (Power BI, Tableau, Metabase, Superset or similar)
* Clear communication: you can explain a result, its limits and what to do about it to a non-technical manager
* English sufficient to present findings and defend methodology
* Professional proficiency in Russian

Nice to have

* Experience in emerging markets or with mobile money data
* Experience with IoT, smart-meter or device data
* Field operations or logistics analytics — routing, depots, delivery efficiency
* Experience with experimentation or A/B testing at scale

What we offer

* Ownership of customer and commercial analytics, and room to shape how it is done
* Direct access to founders and decision-makers; short feedback loops
* Generous AI tooling budget — frontier models are a working expense, not a perk
* Hybrid working from our London office
* Competitive compensation, discussed individually

How to apply

Share your CV and an answer to any of the questions below, at your choice. Applications without answers are not reviewed.

1. After a top-up bonus campaign in one city, the number of top-ups rose 20%, but gas consumed per household barely changed and revenue per household fell. Marketing calls it a success, finance calls it a loss. How would you work out what actually happened, what data would you need, and what would you deliver?
2. Give a real case where two teams or two systems reported different numbers for the same customers, subscribers, revenue or churn. What were the figures, why did they differ, which one did the business treat as truth, and what did you change?
3. Show a real prompt or task brief you gave an agent for an analysis, and what it produced. Then one case where agent output looked right and was numerically wrong: what was wrong, how you caught it, what check you added.
4. Which transactional or customer systems have you personally pulled data from — billing or CRM at a telecom operator, mobile money or payment platforms, smart-meter or IoT data, POS, ERP? Pick one and tell us something about its data that only someone who has used it would know.

Production-ready code in Python and SQL, using AI-code generation and Spec-Driven-Development in a productive & manageable way, familiar with common Data Science & analytics libraries
Data modelling, transformation, and visualization (eg Python Dash)
Experience with software development (modularisation, versioning eg with GIT, tests, understandable code), with containerization (Docker) and orchestration (Airflow)
Habit of starting simple first to get buy-in early and iterate on feedback to add value

Ideally, familiarity with optimization libraries (e.g., Pyomo, SciPy, Gurobi/CPLEX)

# Principal Technical Program Manager, Ring Video Platform

Job ID: 10589011 | Evi Technologies Limited

## Description

The Ring Video Platform Team innovates in the video streaming space for Ring cameras. We are passionate about helping customers see what matters at home, whenever they need to. Every day, millions of Ring devices stream, record and process video through services we build and operate. At that scale we hold ourselves to a high bar for reliability, latency, video quality and privacy.

We're looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to set how our organization plans and delivers its most critical, multi-year initiatives across cloud services, device firmware and mobile apps. You'll partner with senior engineering leaders, programs will escalate to you, and you'll present complex decisions and trade-offs clearly to leaders up to the executive level. You won't be writing production code. You will be expected to read architectures, data and code, with AI help, well enough to tell when a plan, estimate or status is technically wrong, and to test technical trade-offs with evidence.

At Ring, TPMs operate with AI-native fluency: AI tools are a core part of how you plan, execute, communicate and deliver. As a Principal TPM, you'll set the AI-native standards for how programs are run across the organization, decide which tools get built, extended or retired, and define the bar AI-generated output must meet before anyone acts on it. AI fluency that doesn't improve customer outcomes is not enough. You own every output you ship, AI-assisted or not.

Key job responsibilities
- Program Strategy: Set the program execution vision for Video Platform and own the multi-year strategy for its most critical cross-org initiatives, balancing new customer experiences with reliability, privacy, security and cost.
- Portfolio Direction: Own portfolio-level decisions. Greenlight or stop work against clear success metrics, and build the case for what the organization takes on next, not only how it gets delivered.
- Delivery at Scale: Deliver through others. Your success is measured by what the organization ships, not by the programs you personally run. Remove systemic blockers across teams and organizations, and build mechanisms that make delivery faster and more predictable without depending on you.
- Technical Judgment: Test plans, estimates and status against the data. Identify risks and opportunities in architectures, technical strategies and team structures, and make the case for the changes that let teams deliver independently.
- Stakeholder Communication: Write narratives and decision documents that directors and VPs act on. Represent difficult trade-offs clearly in business reviews and escalations.
- TPM Community: Mentor TPMs and engineers, and raise the standard for how programs are run across Ring.
- AI-Native Practice: Design program workflows with AI embedded from the start, including automated status, risk detection, dependency tracking and reusable tooling the organization adopts. When a tool or method falls short, fix the tool or the method, not just its output.

A day in the life
You're shaping several of the organization's highest-priority programs at once. In a typical week you might frame a multi-year delivery strategy with engineering leaders, deep dive into an architecture review to test whether a plan holds up, use AI-generated portfolio views to spot cross-team risks before they become escalations, decide with leadership which initiative to accelerate and which to stop, and improve the agentic workflows the team uses to run its programs. You balance hands-on judgment with long-range planning, and you keep automating the routine so that you and the organization can focus on decisions, strategy and customer impact.

About the team
The Ring Video Platform organization, based in Cambridge/London, builds and operates the cloud services that power Ring video, from the moment a camera starts streaming to when a customer watches it on their phone. We're a collaborative group of teams with deep expertise in video streaming and distributed systems. We invest heavily in how we build, including how we use AI to do it, and we care about spreading that expertise across the organization.

- Experience in technical product or program management
- Experience working directly with engineering teams
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience in architectural design or system design independent of an architect
- Experience in technical program management
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Demonstrated fluency with AI tools in daily work (writing, analysis, reporting, research)

## Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in hands-on work managing complex technology projects
- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience designing AI-assisted or agentic workflows that automate program management work, such as status reporting, risk detection or dependency tracking, and that other teams adopt
- Experience setting standards for how AI-generated output is validated before decisions are made on it
- Experience delivering programs that span cloud services, device firmware and mobile apps
- Experience with large-scale, real-time distributed systems, such as video streaming or media platforms

# Senior NetSuite Administrator & Developer

Cambridge, UK

### **Senior NetSuite Administrator & Developer**

Cambridge, UK | Full-time  | Permanent | Hybrid 

Salary: £58,000 to £70,000 DOE   

### **About us**

Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in material and climate science, to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved.  Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent and passion.  

Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast.  

### **About the role**

Riverlane is looking for an experienced NetSuite Administrator & Developer to define, develop and administer one of the business-critical systems that keeps the company running. 

This is a hands-on role combining day-to-day administration with development and continuous improvement. You'll keep our ERP platform stable, secure and well-configured, act as the senior escalation point for complex issues, and build the scripts, workflows and integrations that make NetSuite work harder for Finance, Operations and the wider business. 

### **About our NetSuite Environment**

We are in the middle of a phased NetSuite implementation, and this role is central to owning and evolving the platform as it grows. You'll be joining as the environment is being stood up, giving you the opportunity to shape how it's run from the outset and ensure the environment has robust configuration, controls and data integrity.

* Phase 1: NetSuite OneWorld across multiple entities and currencies. Scope includes fixed assets, multi-book accounting, currency revaluation, intercompany eliminations, and consolidation.
* Phase 2: Expected to extend the platform with, Advanced Revenue Management for contract revenue recognition, and Inventory Management, including multi-location and serial-number tracking.

### **Key Responsibilities**

**Administration & Configuration**

* Own the setup and configuration of NetSuite, including user roles, permissions, workflows and system preferences.
* Keep configurations aligned with business processes and compliance requirements.
* Perform routine maintenance, manage updates, and troubleshoot issues to ensure system stability and performance.
* Act as the NetSuite subject matter expert, supporting the business, and provide training that helps end-users get the most from the platform in their daily work.
* Maintain data accuracy, integrity and security.
* Manage segregation of duties within roles and permissions to support audit requirements.
* Use sandbox environments and managing NetSuite's twice-yearly release updates.

**Development & Automation**

* Design, build and maintain custom scripts and workflows using SuiteScript, JavaScript and SuiteQL to automate tasks and improve efficiency.
* Identify and implement process enhancements using native system capabilities.
* Ensure delivered solutions are fit for purpose, tested and documented.
* Leverage automations and integrations to enhance the usefulness of the ERP solution and productivity of Riverlane staff.

**Reporting & Insights**

* Design and maintain dashboards and reports using native ERP reporting features.
* Support data transformation and visualisation to inform operational and strategic decisions.

**Security & Compliance**

* Implement and enforce security policies that protect sensitive business data.
* Manage access controls and audit trails in line with standards such as ISO 27001 and Cyber Essentials.

**Collaboration & Optimisation**

* Lead integration efforts between NetSuite and other business platforms.
* Work closely with Finance, Operations and other teams to translate business needs into system solutions.
* Partner with the IT management team on change requests and projects, delivering on time with documented testing and support materials.
* Support the wider IT team with general issues to build overall team capacity.

### **Requirements & Experience**

* Deep, hands-on expertise administering NetSuite — configuration, customisation, migrations, maintenance and troubleshooting — ideally with 3+ years in a comparable role.
* Proficient scripting across SuiteScript, JavaScript and SuiteQL.
* Strong data transformation and reporting skills.
* Experience working with financial data (required), and exposure to ERP implementations or phased rollouts (desirable).
* NetSuite certifications (SuiteFoundation, Administrator, or SuiteCloud Developer) preferred.
* Sound understanding of data security, access control and compliance frameworks (ISO, Cyber Essentials).
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels, with the ability to translate finance requirements into NetSuite configuration and to work effectively across stakeholders (Finance, Operations) and technical teams (developers, integration partners).
* A customer-first attitude, strong project-management discipline, and the ability to juggle multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
* Self-motivated and able to work both independently and as part of a team.

### **What can you expect from us**

* A comprehensive benefits package that includes an annual bonus plan, private medical insurance, life insurance, and a contributory pension scheme
* Equity, so that our team can share in the long-term success of Riverlane
* 28 days annual leave, plus bank holidays and enhanced family leave
* A diverse work environment that brings together experts in many fields (including software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics and maths) and over 20 different nationalities
* A learning environment that encourages individual, team and company growth and development, including a regular programme of learning events and training and conference budgets

### **How to apply**

Please upload a CV and covering letter by clicking 'Apply'. Your covering letter should explain why you are applying for the job and what skills and experience you can bring to the role. 

We review CVs as we receive them and interview as soon as we have applications that look like a good match. We do not use closing dates. So, please apply as soon as possible to avoid missing out on this role. 

If you have any queries, please contact jobs@riverlane.com. 

*Everyone is welcome at Riverlane. We are an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from eligible and suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender reassignment, religion or belief, sexual orientation, marital or civil partnership status, or pregnancy and maternity/paternity.* 

*Women and other underrepresented groups may be less likely to apply for a role unless they meet all or nearly all of the requirements.  If this applies to you, we still encourage you to apply - you may be a great fit, even if you don’t meet every single qualification. We’d love to hear from you.* 

*If you need any adjustments made to the application or selection process so you can do your best, please let us know. We will be happy to help.*

**Job Title:** Support Worker  
**Contract Type:** Permanent  
**Salary:** £28,031.56 per annum  
**Working Hours:** 37.5 hours per week  
**Working Pattern:** 2 weeks rolling rota including weekends and Bank Holiday  
**Location:** Ark House, Parliament Street, Stroud

**The difference you will make as a Support Worker**  
You will be working from one of our supported services providing support to our customers in a variety of ways.  For example, connecting them with employability coaches and other support agencies, helping them manage their money, signing up for benefits or to move on to a more permanent home.

It will be your job to help boost their confidence and support them on their journey as they rebuild their lives.  Through all of this you will need to keep records of everything, so there is some admin to do.  At times this role is tough, but most of the time it can be incredibly rewarding. You will need to be resilient, empathetic, and able to leave your work at work and not take it home with you.

**About you**  
We are looking for someone with:

* Experience of working with vulnerable people
* Experience of delivering structured support and risk management
* To be a team player with a caring and empathetic nature with a resilient, can-do attitude, able to work as part of a team
* An understanding of supporting vulnerable people – this could include having your own lived experience of homelessness or drug or alcohol addiction.
* Ability to work flexible hours to meet customer and business needs, which may not include normal office hours and may include lone working

**Why Riverside?**  
At Riverside, we’re a housing association with a difference – enhancing the everyday for all our customers. For 90 years, we’ve been revitalising neighbourhoods and supporting communities by providing the homes they need to live full, fulfilling and rewarding lives.

We have a portfolio of over 75,000 affordable residential and retirement homes across the UK. Our work ranges from homelessness services to social care, employment support to retirement living, and we need the best people on board to help us.

Working with us, you’ll enjoy:

* Competitive pay & generous pension
* 25 days holidays plus bank holidays
* Investment in your learning, personal development and technology
* A wide range of benefits

**Diversity and Inclusion at Riverside:**   
We are inclusive. At Riverside, we value diversity in all its forms. We foster a workplace where all individuals are respected, empowered, and heard. Our commitment to inclusivity drives our success and enriches the lives of our customers and colleagues.

Riverside is a Disability Confident Employer and operates a Guaranteed Interview Scheme for any applicant who declares they have a disability. If the applicant meets the minimum requirements for the role (as set out in the role profile and/or person specification) they will be guaranteed an interview.

**Applications may close before the deadline, so please apply early to be considered.**

**Role Profile**  
**Support customers**  
We use Psychologically Informed approaches and Trauma Informed Care principles to support our customers to develop new ways of thinking and to make steps towards independence, by:

* Leading on Co-producing bespoke support and move-on plans, involving key stakeholders (e.g. family/other support providers), where appropriate.
* Organising and carrying out regular planned reviews of support and risk plans, or following an incident/significant change in a customer’s circumstances.
* Engaging customers to meet agreed outcomes and develop life skills.
* Assisting customers with day-to-day support and tenancy-related matters.
* Identifying and promoting opportunities for employment, education and training and supporting customers to remove barriers to accessing these opportunities.
* Signposting customers to appropriate external support services, including interventions such as food banks and other community resources.
* Supporting customers to be ‘tenancy ready’ to enable successful move on.
* Supporting customers to be financially independent through budgeting plans and maximising income.
* Supporting and monitoring customers’ healthcare needs, ensuring appropriate contact with healthcare professionals.
* Empowering customers to move towards self-management of their medication by following the medication procedure.
* Leading on support initiatives including Group Work.
* Ensure the safety of our customers by following local safeguarding procedures, recognizing and acting on any significant risk, and escalating appropriately.

* Experience of delivering structured support and risk management.
* Be a team player with a caring, empathetic, flexible and have a resilient, can-do attitude.
* Previous experience in positively resolving incidents.
* Demonstrate initiative and confidence to make and act on decisions.
* Competent administrative and IT skills (to be able to produce reports and other communications).

**Desirable**

* Knowledge of Psychological or Trauma Informed approaches to support.
* Experience of working in challenging environments with the ability to plan, prioritise, organise tasks to achieve results.
* Knowledge of current benefit systems.

Hospitals book relief veterinarians and technicians on Roo every day, and some of those shifts turn into job offers. Relief-to-Hire makes that a product: hospitals try before they hire and pay a placement fee only when a hire happens. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a member of the management team, you'll own the Relief-to-Hire P&L (placement revenue, contribution margin, and the investment decisions behind them) and be accountable for making Roo the way veterinary practices hire, instead of a job ad or a recruiter.

You'll lead a small placement team directly, set priorities for a dedicated product manager and growth analyst, and get much of your leverage from design, engineering, lifecycle marketing and data partners you don't manage. * Design pricing and terms as one system (placement fee, guarantee, payment plans, enterprise caps and lookbacks) and manage the cash cycle from agreement through invoice and collection.

* Build and lead the placement team: hire to a high bar, measure and pay on closed hires and cash collected, act on underperformance early, and develop the people who hold hospital relationships.

### What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you will:

* Grow placement revenue above plan, with contribution margin inside the guardrail agreed with Finance.
* Grow Relief-to-Hire faster than the relief marketplace it's built on.

Description
We're building the UK's next generation engineering powerhouse, providing critical technology that strengthens national security and resilience.

We specialise in turning advances in sensing, AI, and communications into operational capability for the edge, where connectivity may be degraded or denied. Our work focuses on accelerating the deployment of technology, improving decision-making for frontline teams, and protecting people and critical assets in demanding environments.

Headquartered in Bristol, Rowden employs over 200 people and operates over 20,000 square feet of engineering and manufacturing facilities. Recognised in the Financial Times FT1000 as one of Europe's fastest-growing engineering businesses, there has never been a better time to join,

Role purpose 

Rowden is growing, in headcount and in impact. Alongside rapid prototyping and R&D, we are deploying production systems at increasing scale, relied on by customers in demanding operational environments. Our software engineering has to deliver both: the speed to prove new ideas and the depth to turn them into dependable systems.

That growth coincides with a generational shift in how software is built. AI tools are already helping us build, test and develop faster. This is a chance to shape how a growing engineering company works, pairing sound technical judgement with new tools to deliver better software at greater scale.

It’s a rare, potentially career-defining opportunity to join a fast-growing industrial technology company working at the intersection of hardware, software and AI.

Your mission is to build the software function that gives Rowden the speed and capability to deliver, and to set the standard for good software engineering as we scale. Clear vision, disciplined delivery and secure development should be the default, and teams should move at pace without burning out or relying on a handful of individuals.

You will unblock delivery by working directly with teams on hard design, integration, performance and reliability problems, spotting needless complexity and helping find a better way. You will stay technically active where it adds real value and grow strong technical leaders by solving real problems alongside them. You will also step into whichever programme most needs your judgement, while keeping a clear view of capacity, risk and the wellbeing of your people.

And you will shape what comes next. Working with our principal engineers and functional leadership, you will set a clear vision for software engineering at Rowden, covering architecture, practices, tooling and skills, and turn it into a practical roadmap that integrates with hardware and systems practice and holds up as we grow.

Candidates must be eligible for DV clearance.

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels


Key areas of responsibility
This is a functional leadership role with real technical ownership. You will lead the development of our most complex software systems while also building a team with industry leading technical capability through setting high expectations, treating people fairly, rewarding great performance, and making sure engineers have the support to sustain their effort and keep learning.

You need enough depth across these areas to work directly with specialists and challenge technical risk. 

Standards and Capability
Own Rowden’s engineering standards for software: architecture principles, code review, testing, CI/CD and release. Keep them practical and maintained by the people who use them. 
Build a clear path for new joiners and a learning programme for the team, capturing what senior engineers know so it can be taught.
Lead the software vision to the Accelerated Systems Framework (ASF), utilising AI to accelerate development while keeping engineering judgement and accountability with people.
Build commercial awareness: vendor lock-in, open-source licensing, IP and supplier incentives, and how a contract choice can become a technical constraint years later.
People
Run a steady rhythm of 1:1s and performance conversations. Know what every engineer is unusually good at and building towards.
Define team structure and lead roles as we grow, and recruit and onboard with the People team. 
Give engineers exposure to customers, suppliers and operations. 
Track and spot overload early and plan cover and handovers. 
Delivery and Resourcing
Work with the Chief Engineers and VP Engineering to keep delivery on track across our most important programmes.
Own resource planning and flag gaps early. 
Put ‘Just enough’ documented processes in place so delivery is sustainable and change oriented. 
Balance the effect of scope and priority changes on teams before making a decision. 
Assurance and secure development
Make secure by design the default and embed the approach into our SDLC process’.
Drive the development and adoption of our automated test infrastructure. 
Hold lead engineers accountable for the safety and security argument for their functions, with specialists challenging through peer review. 
Build the software assurance roadmap alongside the software principal engineers: test and evaluation, build and release integrity, supply chain, and our position on AI-assisted code and ML assurance.
Knowledge and information management
Own Rowden’s SDLC definition and application end to end, working with the software principals to drive its adoption.


Key skills, experience and behaviours
We expect you to be a strong leader and technically credible in the following areas: 
Architecture and platforms: system design, interfaces, scalability, and the trade-offs that tie architecture to cost and schedule. 
Software Development: Underpinning knowledge of Java, C++, Rust, Python.
Testing, CI/CD and release: automation, configuration management, software at the edge.
Secure development and assurance: Build out and own our approach to secure by design, supply chain risk, and evidence that feeds a Def Stan safety case or Secure by Design artefact set. 
Machine learning and data: MLOps, data provenance, and how models behave outside the lab.
Edge, embedded and networks: embedded software, RF interfaces, and device fleet management in constrained, contested environments.
Commercial literacy: OSS and commercial licensing, IP, switching costs and supplier incentives.
You will be comfortable operating across software, hardware and systems boundaries, developing senior engineers and team leads, and balancing long-term capability building with the demands of live programmes.

## Engineering Manager

Kernel

Software Engineering, Other Engineering · Full-time

London, UK

GBP 130k-170k / year + Equity

Posted on Oct 22, 2026

Apply now

## About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent KERN ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at **Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Checkout** already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 5x YoY.

## **The Role**

You'll be a player-coach engineering leader with a spike in technical strategy, you'll own engineering delivery for your team end-to-end - from developing exceptional engineers to solving some of our most difficult engineering problems & setting technical direction.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll spend roughly 20% of your time contributing code and 80% leading your team, with that ratio shifting as we scale.

## **Key Responsibilities**

* Build, hire, and develop a high-performing engineering team
* Help set technical direction and architecture decisions
* Work with the engineering to tackle some of our most difficult problems
* Own engineering delivery with an emphasis on velocity
* Collaborate closely with Product on roadmap and prioritisation
* Write code when needed so you'll stay close to the product

## **The Opportunity**

We are in the unique situation that our commercial traction is ahead of our product. You’ll play a leading role in moving towards automation in a way that enables us to rapidly scale with increased complexity and specific customer nuances.

## **About You**

* You have extensive experience in architecting enterprise-level systems, delivering on ambitious product visions, and building world class engineering teams.
* You have worked at high-growth businesses, and might have previously started your own company.
* You are highly analytical, and thinking proactively through the implications of your decisions, but also have high conviction and understand the importance of moving at pace and shipping often.
* You have previously led engineering at a company from its earliest stages, and don’t shy away from the manager role - you know what great looks like, and want to help engineers grow.

## **Essential Experience**

* 8+ years software engineering experience
* Track record of hiring and developing strong engineers
* Strong production systems background - you've built and scaled things that matter, and you’ve done something *hard* and lived to tell the tale
* Proven experience in distributed systems
* Experience operating autonomously in small, high-velocity environments - ideally in a startup
* Experience working in a data-focused company or closely alongside a data engineering/ML team - data is core to what we're building at Kernel, and you will play a key role in shaping how we grow that capability

## **Nice-to-Have:**

* Scaled an engineering team through a growth phase (5 → 20+ engineers), or from Series A to Series C
* Technical depth across the stack: NodeJS, Postgres, TypeScript, Kubernetes AI-driven or data-heavy product experience
* Understanding of LLMs (e.g., RAG, prompt engineering, evals)
* CRM data models or workflow automation knowledge
* Hands-on Data Engineering or ML Engineering experience - as data becomes an increasingly large part of what we do, this would be a great asset for us to have

## ⚠️ This role may not be for you if you:

* Insist on shipping pixel-perfect code
* Prefer managing from a distance without technical involvement
* Need extensive process and structure before making decisions

## **❌ This role is definitely not for you:**

* If you over-rely on AI coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code) to the point where you don’t read or understand your own code
* If you on the other hand don’t understand how these tools (Cursor, Claude Code, etc.) can be force multipliers for senior engineers if used correctly
* If you prefer fully remote work
* If you don’t like early-stage startup pace
* If you’re seeking a purely ‘hands-off’ role

## Tech Stack

* **Backend:** AWS, NodeJS, TypeScript, Postgres, Clickhouse, Kubernetes
* **Frontend:** NextJS, TypeScript, Tailwind

You don't need to know everything, but you should be comfortable diving into any part of the stack.

We will do our best to offer you a ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling.

# Residential Experience Manager - Battersea Power Station, London

## Join Battersea Power Station as Residential Experience Manager, bringing teams together to resolve resident issues and deliver clear, consistent updates across the estate.

**Purpose of the Role**

The Residential Experience Manager provides an estate-wide residential liaison and coordination function across all three residential phases. The role ensures that resident matters involving multiple teams are joined up, appropriately allocated, actively monitored and communicated through to resolution, so residents experience a consistent, responsive and well-coordinated service.

The role sits within the Residential team and acts as the principal residential interface with Operations and other specialist functions. It improves visibility, accountability and consistency without duplicating or taking over the responsibilities of Property Management, Operations, Surveying, Technical, PODs, Concierge or other functional owners.

This role is based onsite within the management office, with a requirement to perform certain duties within the buildings around the estate.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Cross-functional coordination and escalation**

- Coordinate complex resident matters that require input from multiple teams, ensuring the right people are engaged and responsibilities are clear.

- Act as the principal residential liaison with the three-phase Operations structure and maintain visibility of issues affecting residents across the estate.

- Track progress on resident-impacting matters, identify stalled, ageing or overdue actions, and escalate delays or unresolved ownership through the appropriate management channels.

- Where matters relate to property management (e.g. lease, financial, project or material reputational implications) they are escalated to the relevant Property Manager.

**Resident communications and experience**

- Coordinate timely, accurate and consistent resident-facing updates for operational matters, maintenance issues, incidents, works and service disruption.

- Ensure residents receive appropriate updates while an issue remains open, including where resolution depends on several teams.

- Work with Property Management and Concierge to support a seamless resident journey and consistent messaging across all the estate.

- Ensure Concierge has the information it needs to support residents, without making Concierge accountable for resolving matters outside its remit.

- Consider the resident impact of operational activity, including access requirements, disruption, temporary closures and changes to services.

- Monitor resident feedback, requests and complaints to identify concerns requiring coordination, escalation or service improvement.

**Residential Portal governance and workflow**

- Act as the Residential portal super-user.

- Oversee the quality of request categorisation, allocation to the correct functional owner, monitoring, updates and closure.

- Review outstanding, ageing and overdue requests; follow up with the relevant owner and escalate where progress is inadequate.

- Maintain clear standards for recording actions, communications, ownership and outcomes so that requests remain visible throughout their lifecycle.

- Produce and use portal management information to identify recurring issues, service trends, response and resolution performance, and opportunities for improvement.

- Reinforce the portal as the primary task-management and tracking mechanism for residential requests, while recognising that direct contact may still be needed during urgent incidents.

**Operational liaison and service insight**

- Maintain a joined-up view of resident-impacting maintenance, operational issues and service disruptions across the estate.

- Liaise with Operations, Technical, Surveying, PODs, contractors, Insurance, Lettings and other relevant teams to coordinate resident-facing actions and information.

- Monitor the residential impact of planned works and projects, ensuring appropriate coordination of access, notices, updates and follow-up.

- Identify recurring operational issues and share evidence-based feedback with the relevant functional owner to support root-cause review and preventative action.

- Provide resident-impact insight into operational performance reviews, while leaving operational KPIs and delivery accountability with Operations and the relevant contract or functional owner.

**Resident engagement and continuous improvement**

- Support resident forums, surveys and other feedback mechanisms where they relate to service delivery and the residential experience.

- Identify patterns in resident sentiment and feedback and translate them into clear actions for the appropriate teams.

- Work with the Residential Services and Operations Coordinator to maintain consistent processes, records, reporting and resident communications.

- Recommend improvements to the residential service journey, cross-functional working and the use of the portal.

- Support a consistent estate-wide residential experience while recognising relevant differences between phases, resident demographics and service requirements.

**Reporting, governance and business continuity**

- Maintain action logs and clear records of cross-functional matters, escalations, decisions and resident-facing commitments.

- Provide regular reporting to the Head of Residential on outstanding and overdue matters, incident coordination, resident feedback, recurring issues, communications and service trends.

- Escalate significant resident impacts, risks, repeated service failures and matters requiring senior intervention.

- Ensure records and handovers are sufficiently clear to maintain continuity during annual leave or absence; work with the Residential Services and Operations Coordinator to provide appropriate reciprocal cover.

- Contribute to clear role boundaries, RACI arrangements and consistent working practices across Residential and specialist functions.

**Skills, Knowledge, and Experience**

**Essential Experience and Skills**

- Experience in residential property, resident services, hospitality, customer experience, estate management or a comparable multi-stakeholder service environment.

- Demonstrable experience coordinating complex issues involving several teams or service providers.

- Strong resident or customer communication skills, including managing expectations during delays, incidents or service disruption.

- Experience using a case-management, property-management, CAFM or similar system to record, track and report requests.

- Ability to monitor actions, identify overdue matters, follow up constructively and escalate appropriately.

- Strong organisation, prioritisation, record-keeping and problem-solving skills.

- Confidence working across operational, technical and property-management functions without direct authority over all contributors.

- Ability to analyse feedback and service information, identify trends and recommend practical improvements.

- Good judgement, professionalism, discretion and an understanding of the importance of accurate records and appropriate information handling.

**Desirable Experience**

- Experience in a large-scale, premium residential or mixed-use estate.

- Experience with Dwellant or a comparable resident portal, case-management or task-tracking system.

- Experience coordinating incidents, maintenance communications or resident-facing activity associated with major works.

- Understanding of residential property management, service-charge environments and the responsibilities of specialist estate teams.

**Personal Attributes**

- Resident-focused and approachable, with a clear understanding of how communication and follow-through shape the resident experience.

- Proactive and persistent, ensuring matters do not lose momentum between teams.

- Collaborative and influential, able to build effective working relationships without overstepping functional responsibilities.

- Accountable and organised, with a strong focus on clear ownership, reliable records and follow-through.

- Calm and decisive when coordinating live incidents or competing priorities.

- Commercially aware and focused on practical, proportionate improvements.

- Committed to consistency, transparency and continuous improvement.

**What Success Looks Like**

- Consistently meeting or exceeding response time and resolution KPIs

- Clear, insightful reporting that drives operational improvements

- Proactive identification and escalation of issues before they impact residents

- High resident satisfaction with communication and service delivery

- Reduced backlog of open requests and improved resolution efficiency

- Strong coordination across teams, ensuring no issues fall through the cracks

**Role purpose**

The Delivery Lead is a coaching-style delivery role that consolidates the different delivery streams across the Enterprise Technology function into a single point of delivery accountability. The role exists to bring consistency, pace and quality to how the function delivers - by coaching teams, raising delivery practice to a common standard, getting hands-on where it adds most value, and holding end-to-end accountability for delivery outcomes across the function.

The role also plays a direct part in the Superhighway programme, Schroders' agentic-development initiative, helping shape and land the way teams deliver in an increasingly agentic engineering environment.

This is a leadership role that leads primarily through influence, coaching and delivery expertise rather than through direct line management alone. **Key accountabilities**

**1. Coach teams and raise delivery to a common standard**

* Identify where teams are below standard and bring them up through hands-on coaching, pairing and practical support rather than mandate.
* Foster a culture of continuous improvement, learning and openness to feedback across delivery teams.

**2. Get hands-on in delivery where it adds most value**

* Step directly into delivery when a team needs it - unblocking, structuring the work, facilitating, or leading a critical piece through to completion.
* Model good delivery practice by doing, so coaching is grounded in credibility and current practice.
* Deploy hands-on effort deliberately and proportionately, keeping the focus on building lasting team capability rather than creating dependency.

**3. Hold end-to-end accountability for delivery across the function**

* Act as the single point of accountability for delivery across the Enterprise Technology function, giving leadership a clear, consolidated view of delivery status, risk and progress.
* Consolidate visibility across delivery streams - milestones, dependencies, risks and run-the-bank commitments - into a coherent picture that supports decision-making.
* Establish and maintain the governance, reporting and decision-making mechanisms that keep delivery accountable, transparent and on track.
* Manage complexity, ambiguity and cross-team dependencies, removing systemic obstacles so teams can deliver.
* Ensure delivery is aligned to the function's strategy, priorities and value objectives.

**4. Play a direct role in the Superhighway agentic-development programme**

* Contribute directly to the Superhighway programme, shaping and landing the delivery approach for agentic software development at Schroders.
* Help teams adopt agentic ways of working safely and effectively, translating new engineering approaches into practical, governed delivery practice.
* Ensure delivery practices scale and adapt as the engineering model evolves, keeping guardrails and standards fit for an agentic environment.

**Experience, knowledge and attributes**

**Essential**

* Substantial experience leading delivery across multiple teams or streams in a technology function, with a track record of raising delivery standards.
* A genuine coaching orientation - able to build capability in others and lead through influence, not just direction.
* Credible hands-on delivery background - comfortable stepping into the detail of planning, facilitation and shipping when needed.
* Strong command of modern delivery practice (Agile and Lean), applied pragmatically rather than dogmatically.
* Proven ability to manage complexity, ambiguity and cross-team dependencies in a large or federated technology estate.
* Confident establishing governance, reporting and delivery transparency for a leadership audience.

**Desirable**

* Familiarity with agentic / AI-assisted software development and its implications for the delivery model.
* Exposure to regulated financial services delivery and its governance expectations.

**Attributes**

* Action-oriented and pragmatic; optimises for outcomes and alignment over process.
* Builds trust quickly and coaches with credibility.
* Comfortable moving between function-level strategy and team-level detail.
* Resilient and adaptable in a fast-changing engineering environment.

* Delivery streams across the function work to a consistent, well-understood standard, with teams visibly more capable over time.

Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm and weekends, no minimum hours. There is flexibility around the start and finish times, volunteers generally volunteer for either a morning or afternoon shift.

🎯 Quality Engineer

🌍 London, N4, expect regular travel to our manufacturing partners in Europe and Asia
